interventions: Placebo control for APT-001 topical ophthalmic ointment

brief_summary: This single-center, single-blind, randomized controlled trial compared two injectates used for ultrasound-guided hydrodissection of the median nerve in adults with carpal tunnel syndrome: autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and 0.9% normal saline (NS). Participants received a single hydrodissection with 5 mL of the allocated injectate per treated wrist; in participants with bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, both wrists were treated with the same injectate. Symptom severity and functional status (Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire), neuropathic pain (DN4 questionnaire), median nerve cross-sectional area on ultrasound, and grip strength parameters were assessed at baseline and at 3 and 6 months after the intervention. The study aimed to determine whether PRP provides benefit beyond the mechanical effect of hydrodissection with saline.
primary_outcomes: Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire - Symptom Severity Scale (BCTQ-SSS)
Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire - Functional Status Scale (BCTQ-FSS)
title: PRP Versus Saline Hydrodissection for CTS RCT

brief_summary: This is a Phase II, single-arm, Bayesian adaptive trial. The study employs a two-stage design with an interim analysis after 30 evaluable patients and a maximum enrolment of 60 patients. T-DXd is administered at 5.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks until intracranial or systemic progression, unacceptable toxicity, or patient withdrawal. SRS (single-fraction) or fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy (fSRT, 3-5 fractions) is delivered within 21 days of enrolment, before Cycle 1 (with a minimum interval of 10 days from local treatment completion and Cycle 1 of T-DXd and a maximum interval of 28 days), for patients with 1-10 BMs and cumulative planning target volume ≤ 20.0 mL.
primary_outcomes: 12-month CNS-PFS rate
title: Study of Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in Combination With Stereotactic Radiosurgery in Patients With HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer and First Diagnosis of Brain Metastases (HERBRAIN)

brief_summary:
This study examined whether taking turmeric extract for 28 days affects oxidative stress and antioxidant defenses in healthy men who practice Muaythai and men who do not exercise regularly. Oxidative stress occurs when reactive molecules exceed the body's protective defenses and can damage cells.

The study included 44 healthy men aged 18-25 years in four groups of 11: Muaythai athletes without supplementation, Muaythai athletes taking turmeric extract, men who did not exercise regularly and received no supplementation, and men who did not exercise regularly and took turmeric extract. Participants were first categorized as Muaythai athletes or sedentary individuals according to their physical activity status. Within each category, participants were randomly allocated to the turmeric supplementation group or the control group using a lottery method.

The supplementation groups received 400 mg of turmeric extract daily for 28 days. The athlete groups followed a structured Muaythai training program. Blood samples were collected on Day 1 and Day 28 to measure malondialdehyde, a marker of oxidative stress, and catalase and reduced glutathione, which are involved in the body's antioxidant defenses. Changes over time were evaluated within and between groups.
primary_outcomes: Change in malondialdehyde (MDA) level
Change in catalase (CAT) activity
Change in reduced glutathione (GSH) level
title: Turmeric Extract and Oxidative Stress in Muaythai Athletes and Sedentary Men

brief_summary: This randomized controlled study was conducted to determine the effects of birth dance on birth beliefs, perceptions of supportive care needs, and anxiety levels in primiparous women. The study will be conducted with primiparous women in the experimental and control groups. The Birth Beliefs Scale, the Scale of Women's Perception for Supportive Care Given During Labor (SWPSCDL), and anxiety level assessments will be used to evaluate outcomes. The relationship between birth beliefs and anxiety levels will be examined.
primary_outcomes: Anxiety and Birth Beliefs
title: Effect of Birth Dance on Birth Beliefs

The study focuses on three anatomical areas: lower back, shoulder, and knee. Participants will be randomized into two arms and will undergo 5 therapeutic sessions.

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to compare the efficacy of two commercially available pulsed field ablation (PFA) systems for catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation. Patients are randomized 1:1 to point-by-point PFA using the CENTAURI PEF system with 3D electroanatomical mapping, or to single-shot PFA using the FARAPULSE pentaspline catheter guided by fluoroscopy and intracardiac echocardiography. The primary endpoint is freedom from documented atrial arrhythmia recurrence between 3 and 12 months after ablation.
conditions: Atrial Fibrillation; Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation; Persistent Atrial Fibrillation

Heart transplant recipients with dual-positive GEP/dd-cfDNA assays with a corresponding negative biopsy between 2 months and 2 years post-transplant will be randomized to treatment with either high-dose oral steroids or placebo, in addition to standard of care therapy.

brief_summary: This multicenter retrospective observational study compares embryological and clinical outcomes following treatment with fresh versus vitrified-warmed donor oocytes at Bocian Fertility Clinic centers in Poland. The study focuses on a standardized allocation strategy in which recipients are intended to receive six mature (metaphase II, MII) donor oocytes. In the vitrified-warmed group, oocytes are cryopreserved at the MII stage and subsequently warmed for use. Oocytes lost during warming are not routinely replaced, allowing the study to evaluate the consequences of warming-related losses within the initial allocation. The study will assess fertilization, embryo development, usable blastocyst yield, the probability of obtaining an embryo for transfer, and live birth following the first embryo transfer originating from the allocated oocytes. Clinical effectiveness will be evaluated from the initial oocyte allocation, including cycles in which no embryo transfer occurs. The objective is to determine whether fresh and vitrified-warmed donor-oocyte strategies are associated with differences in embryological efficiency and the likelihood of live birth when the initial number of mature allocated oocytes is standardized.
primary_outcomes: Live Birth Following the First Embryo Transfer per Initial Donor-Oocyte Allocation
title: Fresh Versus Vitrified-Warmed Donor Oocytes: Embryological and Clinical Outcomes

brief_summary:
Knee osteoarthritis can cause pain, reduced muscle strength, and difficulty with daily activities. Exercise is commonly used to manage knee osteoarthritis, but the effects of different exercise programs on muscle oxygenation are not fully understood.

This study will compare three 6-week exercise programs in adults with knee osteoarthritis: aerobic exercise on a recumbent bicycle, lower-limb strengthening exercise, and a program combining aerobic and strengthening exercise. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the three groups. Each group will attend three supervised exercise sessions weekly for 6 weeks. All participants will also receive a home stretching program. Participants will be assessed before the program, at weeks 3 and 6, and again at week 10, after a 4-week period without supervised exercise.

The study will examine whether the exercise programs improve muscle oxygenation and whether changes in muscle oxygenation are associated with changes in muscle strength, pain, and physical function. The investigators expect muscle oxygenation to improve after the exercise programs and expect these changes to be associated with improvements in clinical measures.
primary_outcomes: Muscle Oxygenation
title: The Effect of Different Exercise Training Programs on Muscle Oxygenation in Individuals With Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary: This randomized comparative clinical trial will evaluate and compare the clinical performance of preformed three-dimensional (3D)-printed resin crowns and Bioflx crowns in children with pulp-treated primary molars requiring full coronal restoration. The study will use a split-mouth design in which eligible children have two comparable contralateral primary molars treated with the two crown types, with the crown allocation to the right or left tooth determined by a computer-generated random sequence. Crown survival will be the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes will include the modified plaque index, modified gingival index, and occlusal wear. Clinical assessments are planned at one week and at 3, 6, and 12 months after treatment.

brief_summary: The left head rotation (LeHeR) maneuver, in which the head of the supine patient is rotated 45° to the left, is a simple, equipment-free technique proposed to improve the laryngeal view. Studies using the Percentage of Glottic Opening (POGO) score during video laryngoscopy have reported improvement with LeHeR, but evidence is limited and the maneuver has not been systematically evaluated in patients with a predicted difficult airway. This prospective, observational, self-controlled study aims to compare the POGO score obtained in the sniffing position with that obtained in the 45° LeHeR position in the same adult patients with a modified El-Ganzouri Risk Index (EGRI) score above 4 undergoing elective surgery under general anesthesia with video laryngoscopy. Ease of intubation, number and duration of attempts, need for adjuvant maneuvers, hemodynamic changes, and airway trauma will also be recorded.
interventions: Video laryngoscopy in the sniffing position
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Glottic Opening (POGO) Score in the Sniffing Position Versus the LeHeR Position
title: LeHeR Maneuver vs Sniffing Position During Video Laryngoscopy in Predicted Difficult Airway

Anterior segment surgery, including procedures involving the cornea, lens, and other anterior eye structures, may be associated with changes in ocular anatomy. SS-OCT is a non-invasive imaging technique that provides detailed images of the anterior structures of the eye and allows quantitative assessment of ocular anatomical parameters.

Patients undergoing anterior segment surgery at Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University, will be included in this study. SS-OCT will be used to assess ocular anatomical parameters, and the collected measurements will be analyzed to characterize anatomical features and explore potential differences among patients undergoing different types of anterior segment surgery.

The findings of this study may improve understanding of ocular anatomical characteristics in patients undergoing anterior segment surgery and provide useful information for clinical assessment and surgical management.

brief_summary:
This single-site prospective observational study aims to validate wearable-derived circadian and behavioral rhythm biomarkers using continuous core body temperature and raw accelerometry measurements and to explore longitudinal changes in circadian and rest-activity rhythms in psychiatric inpatients.

The study consists of two complementary substudies. Study 1 will enroll 150 outpatients and community participants, including 75 patients with major depressive disorder or bipolar I/II disorder and 75 healthy controls. Participants will simultaneously wear a CALERAResearch core body temperature sensor and a Fitbit Charge 6 for approximately 7 days. Agreement between Fitbit-derived circadian and sleep/activity rhythm features and CALERAResearch-derived core body temperature and raw accelerometry markers will be evaluated. A subset of 50 participants will undergo a second measurement at least 1 month later to assess test-retest reliability.

Study 2 will enroll 50 psychiatric inpatients irrespective of final diagnosis. Participants will continuously wear CALERAResearch and Fitbit devices from shortly after admission through the inpatient observation period, with CALERAResearch sensors replaced approximately every 5-7 days. Longitudinal changes in core body temperature rhythms, rest-activity rhythms, and physiological-behavioral rhythm alignment will be examined in relation to changes in psychiatric symptoms.

Circular Correlation Between Fitbit Heart Rate Cosinor Phase and CALERAResearch-Derived CBT Trough Midpoint

Mean Absolute Difference in Phase Changes Between Fitbit Heart Rate Cosinor Phase and CALERAResearch-Derived CBT Trough Midpoint
title: Validation of Wearable Core Body Temperature-Based Circadian Rhythm Digital Biomarkers

brief_summary:
Strokes often induce a motor deficit. The resulting immobilization is in itself an aggravation factor since it worsens the motor deficit induced by the stroke itself.

Amongst the different sensory stimulations, the use of tendon vibratory stimulations (TVS) that activate proprioceptive pathways (muscle spindle fibers) is gaining increasing interest in the rehabilitation world.

Tendon vibratory stimulation (TVS) can be used on patients with little to no voluntary motor functions. Therefore, it seems particularly suited to significant upper limb deficits, and especially as early as possible after a stroke occurs when motor skills are severely affected.

Various studies have shown the interest of using vibratory stimulations in the management of post-stroke motor disorders. The majority were conducted in the chronic stroke stage. Only one small scale study has been conducted on the acute stroke stage.
primary_outcomes: Study whether adding tendon vibratory stimulation (TVS) to the usual rehabilitation sessions on the after upper limb after a stroke improves the recovery of the limb's motor strength.
title: Effect of Early Tendon Vibrations on Upper Limb Motor Recovery After a Stroke

brief_summary: Stroke is a neurological disorder that often causes long-term disability and affects an individual's quality of life. Patients suffering from stroke commonly experience difficulties with balance, gait, and sensory integration due to disturbances in proprioception, postural control, and vestibular function, leading to decreased functional mobility and increased risk of falls. Sensory integration is an essential element of postural stability as it involves vestibular, visual, and somatosensory inputs to maintain orientation and balance. The cervical joint position sense is essential for maintaining balance and spatial perception by providing proprioceptive feedback from the neck region. Vestibular rehabilitation is frequently used to improve balance, gaze stability, and gait disturbance in stroke patients. Although vestibular rehabilitation has shown improvement in stroke survivors, limited evidence is available regarding the combined effects of cervical joint position sense training and vestibular rehabilitation on sensory integration, balance, and gait in subacute stroke patients. The objective of this study will be to compare the effects of vestibular rehabilitation with and without cervical joint position sense training on sensory integration, balance, and gait in stroke patients. The study design will be a randomized controlled trial. Evaluation will be done by using outcome measures for sensory integration, balance, proprioception, and gait, which include the Berg Balance Scale, Timed Up and Go Test, Joint position error, and CTSIB/mCTSIB. The non-probability convenience sampling method will be used, and participants will be randomly assigned to two groups. Group A will receive vestibular rehabilitation in conjunction with cervical joint position sense training and conventional physiotherapy, while Group B will only receive vestibular rehabilitation and conventional physiotherapy. Both groups will receive intervention for 6 weeks, three sessions per week. All outcome variable measurements will be recorded at baseline and once the intervention is completed. The result will be analyzed by using SPSS 27.
interventions: vestibular rehabilitation and cervical proprioception training with Conventional Pt
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: Modified Clinical Test of Sensory Integration on Balance (mCTSIB)
Balance for Berg Balance scale (BBS)
Functional mobility by 10-Meter walk test
CERVICAL JOINT POSITION ERROR (CJPE)
title: Comparative Effects of Vestibular Rehabilitation With and Without Cervical JPS Training in Stroke Patients

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center study will evaluate the feasibility, spatial stability, and dosimetric effects of an absorbable hydrogel spacer placed between the cervix/vagina and rectum before definitive radiotherapy for cervical cancer. Approximately 30 participants will receive hydrogel spacer implantation before the first fraction of external beam radiotherapy (EBRT), followed by standard definitive radiotherapy including EBRT and image-guided brachytherapy (IGBT).

Serial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) will be used to assess spacer position, thickness, and stability throughout treatment. Radiation doses to the rectum and other organs at risk will be evaluated across the full course of radiotherapy. The primary objective is to assess the effect of the hydrogel spacer on cumulative rectal dose while maintaining adequate target coverage. Procedure-related safety and feasibility will also be evaluated.

primary_outcomes: Cumulative Rectal D2cc During the Full Course of Radiotherapy

brief_summary:
The study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of SIM0811 in participants with acute ischemic stroke who are present within 4.5 to 24 hours since last known well. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does SIM0811 improve overall functional outcome, measured by the ability to perform daily activities independently without help 90 days after treatment?
2. What medical problems do participants have when taking SIM0811? Researchers will compare different doses of SIM0811 to a placebo (a look-alike substance that contains no drug) to see if SIM0811 works to treat acute ischemic stroke.

Participants will:

1. Receive SIM0811 or a placebo .
2. Receive standard medical care for stroke. On the first day, all participants will also take an aspirin pill or an aspirin placebo to keep the treatment assignment a secret.
3. Stay in the hospital for a few days to undergo medical tests, including CT or MRI scans and blood draws.
4. Return to the clinic for follow-up visits for up to 90 days to check their recovery and overall health.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients achieving a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-1 at Day 90
title: A Phase II/III Clinical Study of SIM0811 in the Treatment of Acute Ischemic Stroke

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether EP-088\_MM09 works to treat house dust mite allergy. It will also assess the treatment's safety. EP-088\_MM09 contains modified house dust mite allergens called mannan-conjugated allergoids.

The study plans to include 250 participants aged 12 to 65 years. They will have persistent, moderate to severe nasal allergy symptoms, with or without eye symptoms. Participants may also have mild or moderate allergic asthma, provided it is controlled.

The main questions are:

* Does the treatment lower allergy symptoms and the need for symptom-relief medicines compared with a placebo?
* What medical problems or reactions occur during treatment?

Researchers will assess how well the treatment works using a score combining symptoms and medication use. The main assessment will cover four weeks after the treatment course.

Participants will be assigned by chance to receive either EP-088\_MM09 or a placebo. They will have an equal chance of receiving either treatment. The placebo looks like EP-088\_MM09 but contains no active ingredients. Neither participants nor study doctors will know which treatment each participant receives.

Each participant will be in the study for approximately 14 to 21 months.

Participants will:

* Attend one or two visits before starting treatment to check whether they can take part.
* Attend 12 treatment visits, approximately once a month, to receive injections under the skin. They will receive two injections at the first treatment visit and one at each later visit.
* Stay at the clinic for at least 30 minutes after each injection.
* Record symptoms and medication use daily during specified periods.
* Complete questionnaires about their symptoms and quality of life, and provide blood samples.
* Attend a final visit about one month after the last treatment visit.

Participants who are also sensitive to pollen may need a second visit before starting treatment. This is needed if their first visit falls during the relevant pollen season or within one month before or after it.
primary_outcomes: Rhinitis/Rhinoconjunctivitis Combined Symptom and Medication Score (RCSMS) by means of the Subject's Diary
title: Specific Immunotherapy With Mannan-Conjugated Allergoids for HDM-Allergic Rhinitis/Rhinoconjunctivitis. MM09-SIT-063.

brief_summary: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease associated with intense pruritus, recurrent eczematous lesions, sleep disturbance, and reduced quality of life. The disease may be influenced by genetic factors, environmental triggers, epidermal barrier dysfunction, and immune dysregulation. Patients may experience flares triggered by allergens, infections, dry skin, stress, irritants, or other environmental factors. Atopic dermatitis can also be associated with secondary bacterial or viral skin infections and a substantial burden on daily activities, work productivity, sleep, and psychosocial well-being.TREAT is the German national treatment registry for patients with atopic dermatitis. The registry collects real-world data from routine dermatological care to assess disease course, treatment patterns, disease burden, patient-relevant treatment benefits, and quality of life. Data are collected electronically using physician-completed eCRFs and patient-completed questionnaires at inclusion and follow-up visits. The registry aims to improve understanding of atopic dermatitis real-world care and outcomes in daily clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Eczema Area and Severity Index(EASI) score
Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) score
title: ADBest TREAT Registry

brief_summary:

The main question it aims to answer is: does HMB (3 g per day) combined with the Vivifrail multicomponent exercise program improve handgrip strength more than the same exercise program combined with maltodextrin without HMB? Researchers will also compare body composition and physical performance between groups.

Participants will take the assigned supplement every day for 12 weeks, attend three supervised Vivifrail exercise sessions per week at the Casa Club de la Tercera Edad (DIF Tulancingo, Hidalgo, Mexico), and complete evaluations at baseline, week 6 and week 12.

brief_summary:
Acute ischemic stroke occurs when a blood clot blocks blood flow to part of the brain. Patients with this condition may require endovascular therapy, a procedure used to remove the clot and restore blood flow. General anesthesia is sometimes needed during this procedure.

The SAVE trial compares two medicines used for general anesthesia in patients with acute ischemic stroke undergoing endovascular therapy: sevoflurane and propofol. The aim of the study is to determine whether the choice of anesthetic medicine affects the final volume of brain tissue damaged by the stroke.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either sevoflurane or propofol during general anesthesia. The final volume of the brain infarction will be assessed using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) approximately 72 hours after treatment. Participants will also be followed for up to 90 days to assess their clinical outcomes.

The study plans to include 314 participants across seven hospitals in Spain. The results may help improve understanding of how the choice of anesthetic medicine affects outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with endovascular therapy.
lead_sponsor: Fundació Institut de Recerca de l'Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau
primary_outcomes: Final infarct volume on follow-up brain MRI
title: Sevoflurane vs. Propofol for General Anesthesia in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke Treated With Endovascular Therapy

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized pilot study is to determine whether adding expiratory muscle strength training (EMST) to standard pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) is feasible and may help improve stress urinary incontinence (SUI) in females assigned at birth, ages 18 to 79. SUI is urine leakage that occurs during activities such as coughing, sneezing, laughing, or exercising.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Can participants complete the combined exercise program, and is it acceptable to them?

Does adding EMST to PFMT lead to greater improvements in urinary leakage symptoms and participants' perceived improvement compared with PFMT alone?

Does adding EMST improve breathing muscle strength and pelvic floor muscle activity?

Researchers will enroll 24 participants and randomly assign them to one of two groups:

Group 1: Standard physical therapy, including pelvic floor muscle training.

Group 2: The same physical therapy and pelvic floor muscle training, with the addition of expiratory muscle strength training.

Both groups will receive six weeks of supervised physical therapy, with one session each week. Participants will attend seven study visits over approximately seven weeks, including an initial assessment and six treatment visits.

Participants will:

Complete questionnaires about urinary leakage symptoms and perceived improvement.

Have their breathing muscle strength measured using a test that measures how strongly they can breathe out.

Have pelvic floor muscle activity measured using a surface electromyography (sEMG) sensor.

Perform prescribed home exercises and record their exercise completion in a log.

Participants in both groups will practice pelvic floor muscle exercises at home. Participants in the combined-treatment group will also use a device that provides resistance when breathing out. They will perform five sets of five breaths daily, with resistance based on their measured breathing muscle strength.

Researchers will assess whether participants complete the study visits, follow the home exercise program, complete the study measures, and report satisfaction with the program. They will also monitor any unwanted effects related to the exercises or assessments.

The study will explore whether adding EMST to PFMT may improve urinary leakage symptoms, breathing muscle strength, and pelvic floor muscle activity. Participants may experience improvements, but benefits are not guaranteed. The results will help researchers determine whether a larger study is needed to better evaluate this combined treatment for stress urinary incontinence.
primary_outcomes: Attrition

brief_summary:
Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disorder that affects individuals globally, yet there is a significant lack of data regarding its prevalence and management, particularly in Asian populations like Pakistan. To address this gap, we are initiating a groundbreaking project to establish a Lupus Registry in Pakistan.

Our aim is to gain a better understanding of how SLE presents and progresses within the Pakistani population. By collecting detailed information on we hope to provide valuable insights that can tailor diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to suit the local context.

This project will enroll adult SLE patients initially from Fauji Foundation Hospital Rawalpindi, with plans to expand to other centers nationwide. Trained healthcare professionals will collect data through structured protocol as outlined in detailed project description. Through rigorous data collection and analysis, including the use of validated instruments and statistical methods, we aim to delineate clinical features, disease severity, treatment patterns, outcomes, and factors influencing these parameters. Ethical approval and informed consent will be obtained to ensure the protection of patients' rights and appropriate data usage.

This registry will be a crucial step toward addressing the unique challenges faced by SLE patients in our population. Through collaboration and data-driven insights, we hope to pave the way for more personalized and effective healthcare interventions in the future.

The main outcome is complete closure of the perforation at 12 months, assessed by examining the inside of the nose with a small camera. Researchers will also assess nasal symptoms, quality of life, pain in the nose and mouth, and complications.

Swab samples will be collected from the nose and mouth before surgery and from the nose during follow-up. These samples will help researchers study changes in the bacteria present in the nose and whether bacteria found in the mouth before surgery are detected in the nose after repair.

Researchers will also explore whether outcomes differ according to whether the tissue graft was immersed in chlorhexidine, an antiseptic, during surgery. This decision is made by the surgeon as part of usual care, independently of study participation. The study does not assign participants to treatments.

This research will evaluate RM using quantitative measures of symptom burden, pain intensity, sleep quality, and physiological responses among people receiving palliative and end-of-life care in a community hospice. RM will be provided alongside, and will not replace, usual medical and palliative care. brief_summary:
Postural hyperkyphosis is characterized by an excessive thoracic kyphotic curvature and may alter scapular positioning, muscular balance, and upper extremity biomechanics. Scapular stabilizer muscles play an important role in maintaining postural alignment and ensuring efficient force transmission throughout the kinetic chain. Exercise-based interventions, including conventional postural exercises and the Schroth method, are commonly used in the conservative management of postural hyperkyphosis. However, evidence directly comparing scapular stabilizer muscle activation during these exercise approaches remains limited.

The Schroth method is a three-dimensional corrective exercise approach incorporating active spinal elongation, postural correction, rotational breathing, and isometric muscle activation, whereas conventional postural exercises primarily focus on muscle strengthening, stretching, spinal mobility, and postural alignment.

The aim of this study is to compare the activation levels of scapular stabilizer muscles, including the serratus anterior, rhomboids, middle trapezius, and lower trapezius, during Schroth-based corrective exercises and conventional postural exercises in young adults with postural hyperkyphosis using surface electromyography. Isometric muscle strength of the same muscle groups will also be evaluated.

The study will focus on immediate muscle activation patterns during exercise performance rather than long-term treatment outcomes. The findings are expected to provide objective evidence regarding muscle recruitment patterns during different corrective exercise approaches and contribute to the development of more individualized and targeted exercise programs for individuals with postural hyperkyphosis.
primary_outcomes: Scapular Stabilizer Muscle Activation
title: Surface Electromyographic Analysis of Scapular Stabilizer Muscle in Postural Hyperkyphosis

The purpose of this clinical study is to learn about the safety and effects of the study medicine (called PF-08098488) in people with advanced solid tumors (cancer that cannot be removed with surgery or has spread to other parts of the body). PF-08098488 is being studied as a possible treatment for certain types of cancer. These include non-small cell lung cancer, pancreatic cancer, stomach or gastroesophageal junction cancer, and esophageal cancer. This study will also help researchers learn how the study medicine moves through and affects the body.

This study is seeking adults who:

* Have advanced non-small cell lung cancer, pancreatic cancer, stomach or gastroesophageal junction cancer, or esophageal cancer.
* Have received at least 1 previous treatment for their cancer.
* Have cancer that has grown, returned, or is no longer responding to available treatments.

All participants in this study will receive PF-08098488 as an IV infusion (given directly into a vein) at the study clinic. Researchers will study different dose levels and dosing schedules to find the dose that is safe and may work best. Participants will be monitored closely during treatment, especially after their first infusion. They may continue receiving the study medicine as long as their cancer is not getting worse and they are tolerating treatment.

The study includes a screening period of up to 28 days. Participants will have regular visits to the study clinic for treatment and health assessments. These assessments include scans to monitor the cancer and blood sample collection. Tumor tissue samples will also be collected when available or medically feasible. After treatment ends, participants will have a follow-up visit about 1 month later. They will then be contacted about every 12 weeks to check on their health.

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether EP-088\_MM09 works to treat house dust mite allergy. It will also assess the treatment's safety. EP-088\_MM09 contains modified house dust mite allergens called mannan-conjugated allergoids.

The study plans to include 250 participants aged 12 to 65 years. They will have persistent, moderate to severe nasal allergy symptoms, with or without eye symptoms. Participants may also have mild or moderate allergic asthma, provided it is controlled.

The main questions are:

* Does the treatment lower allergy symptoms and the need for symptom-relief medicines compared with a placebo?
* What medical problems or reactions occur during treatment?

Researchers will assess how well the treatment works using a score combining symptoms and medication use. The main assessment will cover four weeks after the treatment course.

Participants will be assigned by chance to receive either EP-088\_MM09 or a placebo. They will have an equal chance of receiving either treatment. The placebo looks like EP-088\_MM09 but contains no active ingredients. Neither participants nor study doctors will know which treatment each participant receives.

Each participant will be in the study for approximately 14 to 21 months.

Participants will:

* Attend one or two visits before starting treatment to check whether they can take part.
* Attend 12 treatment visits, approximately once a month, to receive injections under the skin. They will receive two injections at the first treatment visit and one at each later visit.
* Stay at the clinic for at least 30 minutes after each injection.
* Record symptoms and medication use daily during specified periods.
* Complete questionnaires about their symptoms and quality of life, and provide blood samples.
* Attend a final visit about one month after the last treatment visit.

Participants who are also sensitive to pollen may need a second visit before starting treatment. This is needed if their first visit falls during the relevant pollen season or within one month before or after it.

brief_summary:
Total hip arthroplasty (THA) in patients with complex acetabular anatomy can be challenging because of abnormal bone structure, deformity, or bone loss. Accurate preoperative planning is important for selecting the appropriate acetabular component, determining its position, and achieving stable fixation.

This prospective study aims to evaluate whether patient-specific, CT-based three-dimensional (3D)-printed pelvic models improve preoperative planning in complex total hip arthroplasty compared with conventional radiographic and CT-based planning.

Patients undergoing complex primary or revision THA at Ain Shams University Hospitals will be included. For each patient, two preoperative plans will be prepared. Plan A will use conventional radiographs and CT images, while Plan B will additionally use a life-size 3D-printed pelvic model for surgical planning and simulation.

Both plans will be compared with the actual acetabular component size and orientation achieved during surgery. The study will also evaluate changes in surgical planning, restoration of the hip center, operative parameters, postoperative complications, functional outcomes, and the practical feasibility of 3D printing.

Patients will undergo postoperative follow-up for six months.

The study seeks to determine the additional value of 3D-printed pelvic models in improving planning accuracy and supporting surgical decision-making in complex hip replacement.

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effect of generative artificial intelligence (AI)-supported education in teaching the nursing process on nursing students' learning outcomes. The study was conducted with undergraduate nursing students enrolled in the Nursing Process course for the first time at a foundation university in Istanbul, Türkiye. After a 7-week instructor-centered theoretical course, students were randomly assigned to an intervention or control group using computer-based simple randomization. Over three consecutive weeks, the intervention group worked on three patient case scenarios using a generative AI platform (Gemini), guided by pre-defined themes and prompts covering data collection, nursing diagnosis, planning, and implementation. The accuracy, consistency, and alignment of AI-generated responses with the nursing process steps were then discussed in class. During the same period, the control group completed three different case studies using the instructor's standard care plan template. Nursing process knowledge, self-efficacy in clinical performance, and clinical decision-making confidence and anxiety were measured before and after the intervention, and attitudes toward artificial intelligence and the course were measured after the intervention.

A total of 173 eligible students were randomized (intervention n = 85; control n = 88), and the study was completed with 140 students (intervention n = 68; control n = 72). Students who were repeating the course or were horizontal or vertical transfer students were excluded. The primary outcome was nursing process knowledge, measured with a researcher-developed Nursing Process Knowledge Test. Secondary outcomes were measured with the Self-Efficacy in Clinical Performance Scale, the Nursing Anxiety and Self-Confidence with Clinical Decision Making Scale, and the Attitude Toward Artificial Intelligence and Its Course Scale. Data were collected through electronic forms and analyzed using IBM SPSS 22.0.
primary_outcomes: Change in nursing process knowledge score

brief_summary: Although VNS has been widely used in clinic for over 30 years, its mechanisms of action remain unclear and there is a lack of individual biomarkers of efficacy. One potential and understudied source of variability on the response to VNS may be related to nerve function and recovery following implantation. VNS co-activates the recurrent laryngeal branch of the vagus nerve, which carries vagal-Aα fibres innervating all the laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid. VNS-induced effective activation of the recurrent laryngeal nerve generates a so-called LMEP. Despite the fact that the LMEP represents a simple, non-invasive, and feasible technique to employ in clinical routine, it is not yet sufficiently investigated. This study comprises 5 visits (2 weeks, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months after VNS implantation) and consists of the measurement of the laryngeal-motor evoked potentials induced by vagus nerve stimulation (VNS), that will be further compared with the corresponding clinical response to VNS.
interventions: Increasing VNS Intensities Induced with Magnet

brief_summary: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) is increasingly used for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). This single-center retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with middle thoracic ESCC who underwent esophagectomy with lymphadenectomy (at least 15 nodes retrieved) between June 2012 and June 2025. Station-specific lymph node metastasis rates were analyzed in the NCIT group (n = 272) according to residual pathologic T category (ypT), and in the upfront surgery group (n = 445) according to pathologic T category (pT). The two groups followed different clinical pathways and were not randomized; between-group comparisons are descriptive only and no causal inference is intended. The study aims to provide an anatomic basis for surgical planning and postoperative risk stratification in middle thoracic ESCC.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the impact of an avatar-supported, teacher-student interactive, vodcast-based peer bullying prevention program-developed for adolescents-on students' ability to identify peer bullying, their experiences with bullying, fighting, and victimization, and their levels of empathy.

Designed as a non-randomized controlled study (quasi-experimental), this research will be conducted between October 2026 and December 2026 with students attending two public middle schools under the Ministry of National Education in the city center of Nevşehir. Based on an analysis using the G\*Power (v3.1.9.7) software-with parameters set at an effect size of 0.5, a significance level of 0.05, and a test power of 0.80-the sample size has been determined to be 128 students in total, with 64 students in each of the experimental and control groups. Data will be collected using the "Student Demographic Information Form," the "Peer Bullying Identification Scale (Adolescent Form)," the "Illinois Bullying, Fighting, and Victimization Scale," and the "Empathy Scale for Children," all of which will be prepared by the researcher. During the intervention phase, the experimental group will watch five avatar-supported, teacher-student interactive vodcasts (educational video content), while the control group will receive no intervention. Data analysis will involve the Independent Samples t-test, as well as the Pearson Chi-square and Fisher's Exact tests for categorical data. A Mixed-Design Analysis of Variance (Mixed ANOVA) will be used to compare variables across follow-up time points, and the Bonferroni correction will be applied when comparing main effects. A p-value of \<0.05 will be considered statistically significant; ethical principles will be strictly upheld throughout the study, with a focus on obtaining parental consent and ensuring the voluntary participation of students.

Peer Bullying Scale Adolescent Form
Illinois Bullying, Fighting, and Victimization Scale
Empathy Scale for Children Empathy Scale for Children

brief_summary: This study will be to compare the effects of transcranial direct current stimulation and transcranial alternating current stimulation on neuropathic pain, manual dexterity and isometric muscle strength in diabetic peripheral neuropathic patients. Study design will be randomized clinical trial. Evaluation will be done by using McGill Pain Questionnaire-2, Digital force gauge sf-500 and wooden 9 hole peg board. This study examined how two types of resistance training affect the biceps muscle over six weeks in healthy young men. Participants performed either low-repetition, heavy-load training designed to improve maximal strength or high-repetition training designed to improve muscular endurance. Training was supervised and performed twice weekly.

Researchers measured arm strength and muscular endurance before and after training. They also collected small samples of biceps muscle tissue to examine muscle-fibre characteristics and changes in muscle proteins. These protein measurements were intended to identify early changes in muscle that may occur before visible changes in muscle size or measurable improvements in performance.

The study found no clear differences between the two training approaches in strength, endurance, muscle-fibre size, or muscle-fibre type after six weeks. However, the two programs were associated with different patterns of change in muscle proteins. These findings may help researchers understand the early biological processes through which different types of resistance exercise affect skeletal muscle. This was a small exploratory study, so the results may not apply to other populations or longer training programs.

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate the relationship between everyday cognitive failures and medication adherence in adults with fibromyalgia.

Fibromyalgia is a chronic condition associated with widespread pain, fatigue, and cognitive difficulties such as forgetfulness and problems with attention. These difficulties may affect patients' ability to take prescribed medications regularly, but their relationship with medication adherence remains unclear.

This single-center, observational, cross-sectional study will include 70 adults aged 18-65 years diagnosed with fibromyalgia who regularly take at least one medication for the condition.

Everyday cognitive failures will be assessed using the Cognitive Failures Questionnaire (CFQ), and medication adherence will be assessed using the five-item Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS-5). Anxiety and depressive symptoms will be evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Information on pain severity, medications, and daily medication-taking frequency will also be collected.

The study will examine whether greater cognitive failures are associated with lower medication adherence and whether this relationship remains after accounting for anxiety, depressive symptoms, number of regularly used medications, and daily medication-taking frequency.

All assessments will be completed during a single visit lasting approximately 12-15 minutes. No experimental treatments, additional laboratory tests, or invasive procedures will be performed.
primary_outcomes: Medication Adherence Assessed by MARS-5 in Relation to Pain Severity

brief_summary:
Veterans with co-occurring posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and substance use disorder (SUD) experience significant impairment and worse treatment outcomes compared to those with either condition alone, including higher rates of psychiatric hospitalization, relapse, and suicide risk. Unfortunately, integrated treatment options for PTSD-SUD remain extremely limited despite strong Veteran preference for integrated care over sequential or concurrent models. The only current integrated, evidence-based treatment aligned with VA/DoD clinical guidelines, Concurrent Treatment of PTSD and Substance Use Disorders Using Prolonged Exposure (COPE), requires 12 weekly 90-minute sessions and is associated with a 43-46% dropout rate, with most dropout occurring after six or more sessions. The high treatment burden and dropout rate indicate a critical need to develop a brief, effective, integrated intervention for Veterans with PTSD-SUD.

Written Exposure Therapy (WET) is an evidence-based treatment for PTSD requiring only five 60-minute sessions, with substantially lower dropout than other trauma-focused therapies. The investigators have developed a treatment targeting PTSD and comorbid SUD called RISE (Rapid Recovery through Integrated Substance Use Treatment and Written Exposure for PTSD), that integrates WET with core components of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Substance Use Disorder (CBT-SUD), including functional analysis, urge and craving management, cognitive restructuring, refusal skills, and relapse prevention. By combining these two evidence-based treatments, RISE is designed to reduce treatment burden and dropout relative to existing integrated approaches while addressing both conditions concurrently.

The primary goal of this study is to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of RISE relative to CBT-SUD alone among Veterans with PTSD-SUD. Proposed is a randomized, two-arm pilot clinical trial in which 30 Veterans with PTSD-SUD will be randomized 2:1 to either 1) RISE, an integrated six-session treatment combining WET and CBT-SUD, or 2) CBT-SUD alone, delivered in a matched six-session, 90-minute format. Specific aims include: AIM 1) To evaluate the feasibility of RISE, including recruitment, session attendance, and treatment completion rates; AIM 2) To evaluate the acceptability of RISE using the Client Satisfaction Questionnaire-8; and an EXPLORATORY AIM) To generate preliminary estimates of change in PTSD and substance use symptom severity to inform a future fully-powered non-inferiority trial. If found feasible and acceptable, RISE has the potential to significantly expand access to integrated, guideline-concordant care for Veterans with PTSD-SUD while reducing treatment burden and improving long-term PTSD and SUD outcomes.

Background:

Immunotherapy is a type of treatment that works by making the body s own immune system stronger. These treatments are used for cancers such as non small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); thymic carcinoma (TC); or metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). But these cancers may still come back after treatment.

Objective:

To test a new immunotherapy drug (STAR0602), alone or combined with an approved drug (nivolumab), in people with NSCLC, mCRPC, or TC.

Eligibility:

People aged 18 years or older with NSCLC, mCRPC, or TC that did not respond to treatment or returned after treatment.

Design: Participants will be screened. They will have blood and urine tests. They will have imaging scans and a test of their heart function.

STAR0602 and nivolumab are given through a needle inserted into a vein (infusion). Participants will be treated in 28-day cycles. They will receive infusions of 1 or both drugs on the first and 15th day of each cycle. They will remain in the hospital for up to 5 days after their first 2 infusions of STAR0602.

Imaging scans, blood tests, and other tests may be repeated during study visits. Participants may opt to have tissue samples (biopsies) taken from their tumors. Some blood and tissue samples may be used for genetic tests.

Participants may continue getting STAR0602 for up to 2 years and nivolumab for up to 6 months.

Participants will have an end-of-study visit within 1 month, and follow-up phone calls 1 month and 3 months, after they stop the study drug. Long-term follow-up calls and visits will continue every 3 to 6 months for up to 5 years.

brief_summary:
Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to MUC1 mutations (ADTKD-MUC1) is caused by mutations in the MUC1 gene encoding the protein mucin-1. The most frequently reported mutation is a cytosine insertion causing a frameshift and resulting in the production of an abnormal protein (MUC1-fs). The primary characteristic of ADTKD-MUC1 is slowly progressive chronic kidney disease, with age-dependent progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). Although mucin-1 is expressed in numerous epithelial tissues, including sebaceous glands, the respiratory tract, mammary glands, and gastrointestinal tract, ADTKD-MUC1 is not typically associated with clinical manifestations outside the kidney. The Pafos region of Cyprus is home to one of the largest reported cohorts of patients with ADTKD-MUC1 worldwide, with an estimated prevalence of the MUC1 cytosine insertion of approximately 1 in 580 individuals. The chromosomal region at 1q22 associated with the disease was initially identified by investigators in Cyprus, and the Cypriot cohort has subsequently been extensively characterized and followed longitudinally. ADTKD-MUC1 currently has no approved disease-specific treatment, and most affected individuals eventually develop ESKD requiring kidney replacement therapy, at an average age of approximately 50 years.

Intracellular accumulation of MUC1-fs is considered a major contributor to the pathogenesis of ADTKD-MUC1. Researchers at the Broad Institute, Harvard Medical School, and Massachusetts Institute of Technology developed a high-content screening (HCS) platform using a cell-based immunofluorescence assay to evaluate the effects of approximately 4,500 compounds from the Broad Institute drug repurposing library on patient-derived primary cells. The library included compounds at various stages of preclinical and clinical development, including FDA-approved drugs and supplements. Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) was identified as a compound capable of reducing both wild-type mucin-1 (MUC1) and frameshift mucin-1 (MUC1-fs) protein levels in vitro, as demonstrated by immunofluorescence experiments.

Based on these preliminary findings, the investigators hypothesize that administration of a single high dose of cholecalciferol to patients with ADTKD-MUC1 may reproduce the reduction in MUC1-fs protein levels observed in vitro. Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is commonly used for the prevention and treatment of vitamin D deficiency. The study therefore aims to investigate the effects of cholecalciferol administration on MUC1 and MUC1-fs protein levels in urinary extracellular vesicles collected from Cypriot patients with genetically confirmed ADTKD-MUC1 carrying the MUC1 cytosine insertion mutation.
primary_outcomes: MUC1 and MUC1-fs peptide measurement in urinary extracellular vesicles
title: Effect of Cholecalciferol on Mucin-1 Levels in Urinary Extracelllular Vesicles in Individuals With Autosomal Dominant Tubulo-Interstitial Kidney Disease Due to MUC1 Mutations (ADTKD-MUC1)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical comparative cross sectional study, is to investigate neurophysiological findings and S2PD (static two point discrimination test) measurements after digital nerve injury.

The main aim is to find out if there are measurable neurophysiological differences in fingers following digital nerve injury that correlate with discriminative sensory function (S2PD) as experienced by the patient. Secondary aim is to investigate how well neurophysiological measurements predict specific S2PD values in the affected fingers.

Participants with a sutured digital nerve injury will be examined with neurophysiology and S2PD testing. Both injured finger and corresponding uninjured finger on the other hand will be examined, i.e participants will be their own control.

Prior to the study the investigators will perform a test-re-test study on ten participants to ensure that the method is reliable (separate registration)
interventions: Static two point discrimination test, S2PD
primary_outcomes: Is there a correlation between the amplitude of the sensory nerve action potential and S2PD?
Is there a correlation between sensory nerve action potential area and S2PD?
title: Sensory Neurography and S2PD After Digital Nerve Injury

brief_summary: This first-in-human, open-label, multicenter study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and preliminary antitumor activity of PRT13722, an oral KAT6A protein degrader, in adults with locally advanced or metastatic Hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer. PRT13722 will be evaluated as monotherapy and in combination with fulvestrant, abemaciclib plus fulvestrant, or imlunestrant to determine recommended dose(s) for expansion (RDE) and evaluate preliminary clinical activity.
primary_outcomes: Dose limiting toxicity of PRT13722 (Parts 1A and 2)
Incidence of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events [Safety and Tolerability] of PRT13722 as monotherapy and in combination (Parts 1A and 2)
Preliminary Antitumor Activity: Objective Response Rate (Parts 1B and 3)
title: A Phase 1/1b Study of PRT13722 in Participants With Advanced HR+/HER2- Breast Cancer

brief_summary: This Phase 3 study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of JADE101 compared with placebo in adults with immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). The results will contribute to the overall clinical characterization of JADE101 in this patient population.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the effect of JADE101 on Urine Protein Creatinine Ratio (UPCR) in participants with IgA nephropathy
title: A Phase 3 Blinded Study of JADE101 in Participants With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to use androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) intermittently in hopes of reducing side effects from ADT and reducing unnecessary dosing of ADT in adult men with a prolonged response to frontline therapy for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). The primary aim is to determine the cumulative incidence of participants who experience prostate-specific antigen (PSA) relapse, clinical relapse, or death in the 18-month trial period.

The study will investigate the effects of holding (stopping and restarting as needed) ADT in the participants to monitor time to non-castrate testosterone, quality of life, and outcomes when ADT is only restarted when testosterone is above the castration-level threshold. Androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) will be continued for additional safety. PSA will be monitored throughout to ensure there is no rise. Additionally, quality of life will be monitored throughout to determine whether greater time between ADT doses leads to improvement in side effects.

Participants will:

* See their provider every 3 months
* Check Testosterone and PSA levels every 3 months
* Hold androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) when testosterone remains \<50 ng/dL and resume ADT when testosterone is ≥50 ng/dL
* Continue to take androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) throughout the trial
* Complete Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Prostate (FACT-P) and Hot Flash Related Daily Interference Scale (HFRDIS) surveys
* Undergo imaging throughout the study as clinically indicated, which is consistent with the standard of care
primary_outcomes: To determine the cumulative incidence of participants who experience castration resistance, clinical relapse, or death in the 18-month trial period.
title: Testosterone-Informed De-Escalation in Metastatic Prostate Cancer (TIDE PC)

brief_summary:
People with epilepsy are predisposed to having seizures ("fits"), where abnormal electrical activity in the brain disrupts normal brain functioning. It is a common condition with around 1% of the population of Scotland having this condition. They are treated with anti-seizure medications, drugs which reduce the chance of having seizures.

Unfortunately, people with epilepsy are more likely to have severe infections than those without epilepsy and this is known to increase risk of seizures. The reasons for more severe infections in people with epilepsy are unclear, but one factor may be that anti-seizure medications impair the function of the body's immune system, which fights infection. Our previous work looking at residents in the North-East of Scotland showed a link between these medications and risk of infection.

We plan to study people being started on antiseizure medications (ASMs) with a new diagnosis of epilepsy and those already on ASMs with an established diagnosis of epilepsy in NHS Grampian. We will compare with people not taking ASMs in a group of people with a single seizure and in a group of people with migraine.

We will investigate immune function and infection risk with more-detailed information about individual's background, their seizures/epilepsy, other health conditions, and blood tests. We will then do laboratory experiments to determine how ASMs may impair the immune system by looking at the function of types of white blood cells that play an important part in immune functioning.

We also wish to develop statistical tools which can identify an individual's risk of infection when starting ASMs, based on their demographic, medical and social characteristics, to target closer monitoring/changes in treatment to those with higher risk.

This research will allow us to provide better individualised care in terms of which medication to use for treatment, what doses to use and whether blood tests to screen for impaired immune function would be helpful. We hope that this will lead to reduced risk of infections in people with epilepsy, resulting in better outcomes in this condition.
primary_outcomes: Infections
title: Why Do People With Epilepsy Get More Infections?

brief_summary:
Background: Arthroscopic anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is a common orthopedic surgery. Postoperative pain, inflammatory response and opioid-related adverse events impair early recovery quality. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique with potential analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects.

Participants: A total of 144 eligible participants undergoing ACLR under spinal anesthesia combined with an adductor canal block will be enrolled.

Methods: This prospective, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial will evaluate the effects of perioperative taVNS on early postoperative recovery. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive active taVNS or sham stimulation. Each participant will receive three 30-minute stimulation sessions, scheduled 30-45 minutes before surgery, 6 ± 1 hours after surgery, and 18 ± 1 hours after surgery. All participants will receive standardized multimodal postoperative analgesia. The primary outcome will be the score on the 15-item Quality of Recovery (QoR-15) questionnaire at 24 hours after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include rescue opioid consumption expressed as oral morphine equivalents, pain scores measured using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), functional recovery, and adverse events.

Conclusion: The investigators hypothesize that perioperative taVNS will improve early postoperative recovery quality after ACLR.
interventions: Sham transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation
primary_outcomes: Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score
title: Effect of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Postoperative Recovery Quality in Patients Undergoing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction

brief_summary: A multicenter prospective study to evaluate the clinical performance, usability, and contrived result interpretation of the INSTI® HCV Antibody Test (INSTI HCV) with fingerstick (FS) whole blood specimens from participants with signs or symptoms of hepatitis or participants at risk for hepatitis C infection, by trained operators at point of care (POC) settings. POC settings are locations where medical diagnostic testing is performed at or near the site of patient care.
primary_outcomes: Performance Evaluation
title: Study to Evaluate the Performance of the INSTI® HCV Antibody Test for Point-of-Care Use in Individuals at Risk for HCV Infection or Presenting With Signs or Symptoms of HCV Infection

brief_summary:
This study evaluates the effects of Primal Harvest's Primal Meno+ supplement on symptoms of menopause and overall well-being in females aged 40-60 who are currently menopausal and experiencing at least two menopausal symptoms. Over a 12-week period, 40 participants will take one capsule of the test product daily with their first meal of the day.

Participants will complete self-reported questionnaires at Baseline, Week 4, Week 8, and Week 12 to assess menopausal symptoms (including hot flashes, night sweats, sleep quality, stress resilience, and emotional well-being) and overall health and well-being. This is a single-arm, open-label, virtual trial with no randomization or blinding.

Change in Hot Flashes
Change in Night Sweats

Change in Sleep Quality
Change in Emotional Well-being

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine the effectiveness of oropharyngeal suction in detecting microorganisms by comparing it with induced sputum and oropharyngeal swab samples. It also aims to assess the effect of respiratory physiotherapy on improving the results obtained in children aged 5-18 years with chronic lung disease.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What is the diagnostic efficacy of oropharyngeal suction in detecting microorganisms compared with induced sputum?
* What is the effect of undergoing a physiotherapy session before sample collection?
* How do the results obtained from oropharyngeal suction correlate with those obtained from oropharyngeal swabs?
* How does the age of the participants affect the results obtained from each sampling technique and the effect of prior physiotherapy?
* Are these techniques safe?

Researchers will compare samples collected after a physiotherapy session with those collected without prior physiotherapy to determine whether physiotherapy improves culture results.

Participants will be randomized into two groups: one group will undergo a physiotherapy session before sample collection, while the other will not. Three samples will be collected from each participant using oropharyngeal suction, an oropharyngeal swab, and induced sputum. Each participant may take part on multiple occasions, provided that at least one month has elapsed since their previous participation. On each occasion, participants will be randomized again.
primary_outcomes: Presence/absence of microorganisms in each sample, as a binary variable
title: Diagnostic Value of Oropharyngeal Suction and Effect of Respiratory Physiotherapy on the Detection of Microorganisms in the Pediatric Patient

brief_summary: Since 2019, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has led family planning programming in Somalia under the Women's Integrated Sexual Health (WISH) program, funded by the United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. This study will assess contraceptive and gender-norms outcomes in communities in Galgaduud region, where the IRC implemented WISH-1 (2019-2025) and continues programming under WISH-2. Approximately one year into WISH-2 implementation, the IRC will add gender-transformative programming, which this study will evaluate over the subsequent two years. The intervention aims to change harmful gender norms that constrain women's family planning decision-making, through programming with women, men, couples, and communities; the IRC will implement an intensive and a light-touch version. This study is independent of the IRC and is one of four studies in the Guttmacher Institute's Family Planning Impact Lab (FPIL), which produces experimental research estimating the causal impact of family planning interventions on women's health, wellbeing, and development outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Change in the proportion and number of women using preference-aligned fertility management between baseline, midline, and endline
Change in men's agreement with the statement "A husband should have the final say about whether his wife uses contraception," between baseline, midline, and endline
Change in the proportion and number of women aged 15 to 49 using a modern contraceptive method (modern contraceptive prevalence) between baseline, midline, and endline
title: Impact of Gender-Transformative Interventions on Contraceptive Use and Reproductive Autonomy in Somalia

brief_summary:
This study will examine the short-term safety and tolerability of NRICM301, a food-grade herbal formula also known as Taiwan Xingnao No. 1, when added to standard care for adults hospitalized with acute ischemic stroke. An ischemic stroke occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked.

The study will enroll up to 45 adults at Tri-Service General Hospital in Taiwan. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either NRICM301 or a matching placebo for 14 days. Both groups will continue to receive standard stroke care. The study drink will be given by mouth or through a nasogastric tube, starting within 24 hours after hospital arrival. Participants and the study personnel involved in treatment and assessments will not know which study product each participant receives.

The main question is whether the proportion of participants who experience an adverse event considered at least possibly related to the study product differs between the two groups through Day 15. The study will also assess blood test results, neurological function, ability to perform daily activities, hospital and intensive care use, and inflammation markers. Follow-up is planned through Day 91. This is an exploratory safety study; it is not designed to establish definitive treatment effectiveness.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Study Product-Related Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events
title: Safety of NRICM301 Added to Standard Care in Adults With Acute Ischemic Stroke

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and preliminary antitumor activity of BON-C1393 monotherapy or in combination with other anticancer regimens in adults with selected advanced solid tumors. The study will consist of Phase 1a (Dose Escalation and Dose Exploration) and Phase 1b (Dose Expansion).
primary_outcomes: Phase 1a: Number of Participants with Dose-Limiting Toxicities (DLTs)
Phase 1a: Number of Participants with Treatment-emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs), Treatment-related Adverse Events (TRAEs), and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
Phase 1b: Overall Response Rate (ORR) Assessed by the Investigator
title: A Study of BON-C1393 in Adults With Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial compared early outcomes after replacement of both knees during the same operation, with and without tourniquet use. A tourniquet was an inflatable cuff placed around the upper thigh and tightened during surgery to temporarily restrict blood flow. The study tested the hypothesis that tourniquet use would reduce blood loss during and after surgery, preserve hemoglobin levels, and reduce early postoperative pain. Hemoglobin was the protein in red blood cells that carried oxygen.

The study was designed to include 84 patients aged 40-80 years at the Department of Orthopedic Surgery, Shifa International Hospital, Islamabad. Patients were randomly assigned to two equal groups of 42. One group underwent replacement of both knees with tourniquet use, while the other underwent the same procedure without tourniquet inflation. Both groups received standardized surgical care, pain management, blood clot prevention, and rehabilitation.

The outcomes assessed were blood loss during surgery, blood collected through drains from both knees during the first 24 hours after surgery, hemoglobin levels at 24 hours, and the decrease from preoperative hemoglobin levels. Pain in each knee was assessed at 24 and 48 hours using a scale from 0, indicating no pain, to 10, indicating the worst possible pain. These measurements were compared between the two groups to assess the effect of tourniquet use on early recovery.
interventions: Simultaneous Bilateral Total Knee Replacement with Tourniquet
Simultaneous Bilateral Total Knee Replacement without Tourniquet
primary_outcomes: Intraoperative Blood Loss
title: Early Outcome of Simultaneous Bilateral Total Knee Replacement With and Without Tourniquet

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding a small amount of blood taken from the jawbone marrow improves new bone formation when two different bone graft materials are used in maxillary sinus lift surgery. The study includes adults aged 25 to 65 who need more bone height in the upper back jaw before receiving dental implants.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does InterOss (a bovine bone graft material) form a similar amount of new living bone as Bio-Oss (a widely used bovine bone graft material)?
* Does mixing either graft material with bone marrow blood from the lower jaw increase the amount of new living bone and the bone height gained?

Researchers will compare four groups: Bio-Oss alone, InterOss alone, Bio-Oss mixed with jawbone marrow blood, and InterOss mixed with jawbone marrow blood. Each treated sinus is randomly assigned to one group. Patients treated on both sides receive a different treatment on each side.

Participants will:

* Have a sinus lift surgery through a small side window in the upper jaw, where the sinus floor is filled with the assigned graft material. In two of the groups, a small amount of marrow blood (about 0.5 mL) will be drawn from the lower jaw and mixed with the graft.
* Have a 3D dental X-ray (cone beam CT) before surgery and 8 months after surgery to measure the bone height gained.
* Have dental implants placed 8 months after the sinus lift. During this surgery, a small bone sample will be taken from the grafted area and examined under a microscope.
* Receive their implant-supported teeth about 6 months later and attend yearly check-up visits with a clinical exam and X-rays.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of New Vital Bone in the Augmented Sinus
title: Two Bovine Xenografts in Lateral Window Sinus Augmentation With or Without Bone Marrow Blood

brief_summary:
This is a single-center, single-arm, phase II clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of becotatug vedotin combined with gemcitabine and a PD-1 inhibitor as second-line or later treatment for patients with recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) who have experienced treatment failure following prior platinum-based chemotherapy or PD-(L)1 inhibitor therapy.

Patients with recurrent or metastatic NPC who are unsuitable for curative local treatment and meet the eligibility criteria will receive becotatug vedotin, gemcitabine, and a PD-1 inhibitor every 3 weeks for 4-6 cycles, followed by PD-1 inhibitor maintenance therapy until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

Approximately 30 patients will be enrolled. The primary objective is to evaluate the objective response rate (ORR) according to RECIST version 1.1. Secondary objectives include evaluating disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and treatment safety.

This study aims to explore a potential treatment option for patients with recurrent or metastatic NPC who have limited therapeutic options after failure of previous systemic therapy.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR)
title: Becotatug Vedotin Plus Gemcitabine and a PD-1 Inhibitor in Recurrent or Metastatic Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether blood vessel health and function differ between adults aged 40 years or older with cystic fibrosis (CF) who are taking CFTR modulator therapy and healthy adults of the same age and sex. As people with CF now live longer, they may face a higher risk of heart and blood vessel disease and stroke.

The main question it aims to answer is:

Is the function of the arteries in the arm (measured by radial artery flow-mediated dilation and low-flow mediated constriction) reduced in people with CF compared with healthy controls?

Researchers will also compare the function of the neck (carotid) arteries, blood flow control in the brain, the reflexes that control blood pressure, and blood markers of inflammation and oxidative stress between the two groups. They will also look at whether these measures relate to memory and thinking, mood, and quality of life.

Participants will attend a single study visit of about 2.5 to 3 hours at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital (or Manchester Metropolitan University for some healthy controls). During the visit they will:

* Have height, weight, waist and hip size and body fat measured
* Give a blood sample
* Have ultrasound scans of the arm and neck arteries, including a short period with a blood pressure cuff inflated on the wrist and a few minutes with one hand in cold water
* Have brain blood flow, heart rhythm, blood pressure and breathing monitored while resting, lying, standing, doing repeated squats and opening and closing their eyes
* Complete short tests of memory and thinking, and questionnaires about mood and quality of life
interventions: Non-invasive vascular, cerebrovascular and autonomic assessment
lead_sponsor: Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
primary_outcomes: Radial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD)
Radial artery low-flow mediated constriction (L-FMC)
title: Vascular Health and Function in Cystic Fibrosis

brief_summary:
After knee or hip replacement surgery, rehabilitation helps patients regain mobility, improve muscle strength, and return to their daily activities.

The TELEARTHROPOSTOP-G/H study aims to evaluate whether telerehabilitation, using a digital application at home, can improve physical function after knee or hip replacement surgery compared with usual rehabilitation alone.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will receive standard rehabilitation during their stay at the Institut Stablinski rehabilitation center, including physiotherapy sessions and adapted physical activity sessions.

Participants in the usual rehabilitation group will continue their rehabilitation independently at home after discharge, following standard practice. Participants in the telerehabilitation group will receive the same care and will also be trained to use a digital application before leaving the rehabilitation center. At home, they will be able to follow exercise videos selected by their therapist. The exercises can be adjusted over time to match their recovery.

All participants will be asked to complete questionnaires about pain, joint function, physical activity, and quality of life. These questionnaires will be completed at the beginning of the study and again approximately 6 weeks and 3 months after surgery. Follow-up questionnaires will be completed remotely, by telephone or email.

Participation in the study will last up to 3 months. The study aims to determine whether adding telerehabilitation to usual care can help patients recover their physical function after knee or hip replacement surgery.
primary_outcomes: Total WOMAC Score at 6 Weeks Postoperatively
title: Comparison of Telerehabilitation and Usual Rehabilitation After Knee or Hip Surgery

brief_summary: The Oral Health Impact Profile for Edentulous Patients (OHIP-EDENT-19) is a 19-question survey about how complete tooth loss and dentures affect daily life. This study will translate and culturally adapt the questionnaire into Russian and assess its validity and reliability in Russian-speaking adults who have lost all teeth in both jaws and wear complete removable dentures. The study includes cognitive interviews with up to 30 participants and a psychometric assessment in 300 participants. A subgroup of 60-80 clinically stable participants will complete the questionnaire again after 10-14 days. No treatment is assigned or changed; participation involves questionnaires, interviews, and collection of limited demographic and clinical information.
lead_sponsor: St. Petersburg State Pavlov Medical University
primary_outcomes: Structural Validity of OHIP-EDENT-RU Assessed by Confirmatory Factor Analysis
title: Russian Version of OHIP-EDENT-19 for Adults With Complete Tooth Loss

brief_summary: The study aims to determine the acute efficacy and safety of three sequential doses of acetazolamide (62.5 mg, 125 mg, 250 mg) each for 2 weeks in 20 patients with T2D receiving background SGLT2i therapy.
primary_outcomes: Iohexol Measured GFR
