brief_summary:
Obstructive ventilatory disorders, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, and pulmonary emphysema, are chronic conditions characterized by progressive airflow limitation and worsening dyspnea, leading to increasing restrictions in daily activities and quality of life.

Although these diseases are not curable, early diagnosis and appropriate treatment can slow disease progression, reduce exacerbations, and preserve functional capacity and well-being. Adherence to prescribed inhaled therapies is therefore essential from the earliest stages of the disease. However, both clinical experience and published evidence suggest that many patients with COPD and asthma experience poor disease control, relapses, and exacerbations due to inadequate inhaler use and suboptimal treatment adherence.

Previous research has explored treatment satisfaction among patients with COPD and examined perceptions and beliefs regarding pharmacological therapies in other chronic conditions, such as diabetes, depression, and autoimmune diseases. Studies have also highlighted the importance of adopting a patient-centered approach when selecting inhaler devices based on individual patient characteristics. Nevertheless, little is known about how patients with obstructive ventilatory disorders perceive inhaled therapies and their role in disease management.

The aim of this study is to investigate patients' perceptions of inhalation therapy, focusing on factors that influence its use, the value attributed to inhaled medications, preferences regarding the route of administration, awareness of the underlying disease, perceived barriers to treatment, and beliefs about medications in general.

Understanding how patients perceive both the treatment and its route of administration is a key component of patient engagement, which emphasizes patients' active involvement in managing their health and healthcare pathway.

Currently, no validated tools, either internationally or in Italian, are specifically designed to assess perceptions of the usefulness and effectiveness of inhalation therapy in patients with obstructive ventilatory disorders. This study therefore aims to address an important gap in the literature and support the development of more patient-centered therapeutic strategies.
primary_outcomes: AUDIT
title: Perception of the Benefits and Effectiveness of Inhalation Therapy in Patients With Obstructive Dyspnea

brief_summary: Kidney stones are common and often come back. One reason may be that some people with calcium stones have low phosphate levels in the blood and lose too much phosphate through the kidneys. They may also have high calcium in the urine, which raises the chance of forming stones. In older studies, high doses of phosphate supplements lowered urine calcium and appeared to reduce stone formation, but they sometimes caused stomach and bowel side effects, and phosphate is no longer used for stone prevention. This small pilot study will test a much lower dose of neutral phosphate (250 mg twice daily) for 2 weeks in adults with recurrent calcium oxalate kidney stones, high urine calcium, and low blood phosphate. Participants will collect a 24-hour urine sample and have blood drawn before and after the 2-week period. The study will look at whether the low dose reduces urine calcium and the risk of stone formation in urine. The results will help decide whether a larger study is warranted.
primary_outcomes: Change in from urine calcium from baseline (time 0) and 2-weeks (completion) after oral phosphate (250mg twice daily) supplementation
title: Phosphate & Kidney Stones

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn how hot indoor temperatures affect mood in young adults with depression, with or without anxiety. It will also explore whether the time of day the heat happens matters, and whether changes in sleep, thinking, and daily activity help explain the effect.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does heat during the day affect mood differently than heat at night?
* Do changes in sleep, thinking, or activity help explain those effects? Researchers will compare a weekend that is hot during the day to a weekend that is hot at night to see how the timing of heat affects mood.

Participants will take part for about four weeks. During that time, participants will:

* Stay in a sleep lab for two weekends, two weeks apart. Each stay runs from Friday afternoon to Monday midday.
* Spend one weekend in rooms that are hot (32°C, or 90°F) from 8 in the morning to 8 at night, and comfortable (22°C, or 72°F) overnight
* Spend the other weekend in rooms that are comfortable (22°C, or 72°F) during the day and hot (32°C, or 90°F) overnight
* Be woken up at 2 in the morning on the last night of each lab stay. Participants will answer questions and do short thinking tasks, then go back to sleep.
* Wear sensors that track their sleep, heart rate, and body temperature, and swallow a small capsule that measures body temperature from the inside
* Answer questions about their mood and do short thinking tasks, both in the lab and at home
* Use a phone app for the whole four weeks of the study. The app asks about mood and sleep, and works with the sensors to track sleep, movement, heart rate, temperature, and humidity.
primary_outcomes: PANAS-10
POMS-8 [depression subscale of POMS-60]
PHQ-9
GAD-7
Qualitative Experience
title: Heat and Mental Health - PART 2

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate how well first-line immunotherapy works and investigate its association with immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in Egyptian adults with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a type of liver cancer that cannot be removed by surgery.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Are immune-related adverse events (irAEs), which are side effects caused by activation of the immune system, associated with treatment response and survival?
* How effective and safe is first-line immunotherapy in Egyptian patients with unresectable HCC?

The study will also explore whether routine blood markers, including eosinophil counts and markers of inflammation and nutritional status, are associated with treatment outcomes and the development of immune-related side effects. Changes in liver function and patients' health-related quality of life will also be evaluated.

Approximately 294 patients receiving first-line immunotherapy as part of their routine medical care will be included. Patients may receive atezolizumab plus bevacizumab or durvalumab plus tremelimumab, as prescribed by their treating physicians. Researchers will not assign treatments or change patients' medical care.

The study will include a review of existing medical records and prospective follow-up of eligible patients. Researchers will:

* Review medical records to collect information about treatment, routine blood tests, imaging results, side effects, and clinical outcomes.
* Follow eligible patients during routine medical visits to assess treatment response, survival, adverse events, and changes in liver function.
* Ask prospectively enrolled participants to complete questionnaires about their health-related quality of life during scheduled follow-up assessments.

Researchers will compare treatment outcomes between patients who develop irAEs and those who do not, while taking into account when these side effects occur.
primary_outcomes: Odds Ratio for Objective Tumor Response According to Immune-Related Adverse Event Status (RECIST 1.1)
Hazard Ratio for Overall Survival According to Time-Varying Immune-Related Adverse Event Status
title: Immune-Related Adverse Events and Clinical Outcomes of First-Line Immunotherapy in Egyptian Patients With Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma

Part 1 evaluates single ascending intravenous (IV) doses (SAD) and optional subcutaneous (SC) doses. Part 2 evaluates multiple ascending subcutaneous doses (MAD). brief_summary: This research aims to evaluate the impact of a cancer awareness education program (Cancer Awareness Programme Via Digital Health Literacy - DigiCAP), designed to enhance digital literacy and applied to stroke patients, on uncertainty, anticipatory anxiety, and cancer awareness. This study was designed as a randomized controlled, single-blind (evaluator-blind), pre-test-post-test experimental design. In the study, all individuals in the sample group were administered the Personal Information Form, the Mishel Illness Uncertainty Scale-Community Form (MIIS-T), the Beck Anxiety Scale (BAS), and the E-Health Literacy Scale as pre-test applications. The training program prepared for the experimental group will be presented. Final tests will be conducted at the end of the training. Individuals will be contacted by phone one month after the training for reminder purposes. Individuals are expected to participate in cancer screening within 3 months.
primary_outcomes: DATA COLLECTION

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial was designed to evaluate the effects of concurrent instructionally irrelevant visual stimuli on learning-related outcomes among third-year midwifery students. Participants were assigned to either a split-screen educational condition or a standard instructional condition. Both groups received the same 45-minute theoretical session on delivery-room management of the newborn. The intervention group was exposed to an unrelated soap-cutting video displayed concurrently with the educational presentation, whereas the control group received standard PowerPoint-supported instruction. The primary outcome was attitude toward learning. Secondary outcomes included theoretical knowledge, state anxiety, academic motivation, and satisfaction with the teaching method. Outcomes were assessed immediately after the educational session.

brief_summary:
Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disease that can cause pain, stiffness, and reduced functional performance in the wrist and hand joints. These problems may make daily activities, such as gripping objects and performing self-care tasks, more difficult.

The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effects of paraffin wax therapy and dry cupping on pain intensity and wrist joint functional performance among patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The study will compare two groups: one receiving paraffin wax therapy and the other receiving dry cupping therapy

Pain intensity and wrist joint functional performance will be assessed before and after the interventions using standardized assessment tools. The findings may help determine whether these complementary therapies can reduce pain and improve wrist function in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
primary_outcomes: Change in Pain Intensity Measured by the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: Effects of Paraffin Wax Therapy and Dry Cupping on Pain and Wrist Function in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis

brief_summary:
This is a phase 1, multicenter, open-label, single-arm study evaluating SND002 Cell Injection in participants with advanced malignant solid tumors that have progressed after standard treatment or for whom no standard treatment is available.

SND002 Cell Injection is an investigational product made from a participant's own immune cells (T cells). These cells are collected from a lymph node that drains the tumor, expanded in a laboratory, and then given back to the same participant by intravenous infusion. Because the cells come from the participant, the approach is intended to help the participant's immune system recognize and attack the tumor.

The study has two parts. In Part A, small groups of participants receive increasing numbers of cells to identify the dose range that is safest and best tolerated. In Part B, additional participants with colorectal cancer, gastric cancer, or other solid tumors receive the dose range selected in Part A, to learn more about antitumor activity.

Before the infusion, participants receive a short course of chemotherapy to prepare the body for the cells. After the infusion, participants receive interleukin-2 injections for several days and are monitored closely. Safety is assessed for 28 days after the infusion, and participants are then followed for up to 1 year to assess tumor response and survival.

The main questions are (1) what side effects occur, how severe they are, and what dose range is recommended for further study, and (2) in the expansion part, how many participants experience a reduction in tumor size.

Approximately 69 to 78 participants will be enrolled at multiple hospitals in China. Follow-up continues for up to 1 year after the infusion.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, and dose-limiting toxicities
Recommended cell-dose range (cells) for further study as determined by the Safety Review Committee
Percentage of participants with an objective response (complete response or partial response) assessed by RECIST 1.1
Percentage of participants with disease control (complete response, partial response, or stable disease) assessed by RECIST 1.1
title: SND002 Cell Injection in Participants With Advanced Malignant Solid Tumors

brief_summary:
This is a phase I, open-label, non-randomized clinical trial that will enroll pediatric and adult research participants with CLEC2A+ acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that does not go away with treatment (is refractory) or comes back after treatment (is recurrent). The goal is to evaluate the safety, feasibility, and efficacy of administering T cell products (modified immune cells) derived from the research participant's blood that have been genetically modified to express chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) targeting SC-CAR.CLEC2Av1. The main questions it seeks to answer are:

* How safe is the T cell product infusion (modified immune cells)?
* How feasible is it to manufacture the cell products? Participants will first receive treatments to prepare their body (bridging therapy and lymphodepletion). On Day 0, they receive a single infusion of CLEC2A CAR T cells, which are modified immune cells designed to target and fight cancer.

Researchers will evaluate the safety and side effects of the treatment, check how well the CAR T cells survive and multiply in the body over time (using blood, bone marrow, and cerebrospinal fluid samples), and assess how well the treatment fights the AML. Bone marrow tests are performed on Day 28 to check the response.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants experiencing Dose Limiting Toxicities (DLTs) and treatment-related adverse events as assessed by NCI CTCAE v6.0, ASTCT CRS/ICANS scales, and IEC-HS grading.
The feasibility of manufacturing SC-CAR.CLEC2Av1 CAR T cells from children and adults with relapsed or refractory CLEC2A+ AML.
title: A Study of CLEC2A CAR T for Pediatric and Adult Patients With Relapsed or Refractory AML

brief_summary:
Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a severe inflammatory complication that can occur after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Its signs can overlap with those of infection and other transplant complications, making early recognition difficult. This study will examine whether changes in routine blood tests and clinical information can help identify patients who may develop HLH during the following seven days.

The study will combine a review of existing medical records with prospective follow-up at participating hospitals in China. Approximately 20,000 adults undergoing their first allogeneic transplantation will be included, with approximately 400 post-transplant HLH cases expected. Historical records will be used to develop the prediction model. Data from independent centers and prospectively enrolled patients will be used to validate the model.

Participants will be followed for one year after transplantation. Those who develop HLH during that year will also be followed for 90 days after HLH onset. The study will describe HLH occurrence, associated factors, treatments, and survival. All tests and treatments will remain part of routine care. No additional research samples or laboratory tests will be required, and model predictions will not be used to guide treatment.
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Incidence of First De Novo HLH Within 365 Days After Transplantation
Discrimination of the 7-Day HLH Risk Prediction Model
Calibration of Predicted 7-Day HLH Risk
Positive Predictive Value of 7-Day HLH Alerts
Case Detection Rate for Incident HLH
title: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis After Allogeneic Stem Cell Transplantation

brief_summary:
This study investigated the effects of paracetamol administration on oxidative stress in children undergoing inguinal hernia surgery under sevoflurane-based general anesthesia.

Oxidative stress occurs when the production of potentially harmful molecules exceeds the body's antioxidant defenses. Anesthesia and surgery may influence this balance.

The study compared two groups of children who received intravenous paracetamol at different stages of anesthesia. In one group, paracetamol was administered before premedication with midazolam and induction of anesthesia with sevoflurane. In the other group, paracetamol was administered after midazolam premedication and induction of anesthesia.

Blood samples were collected at four predefined time points to measure markers of oxidative stress and antioxidant defense.

The aim was to determine whether the timing of paracetamol administration influenced oxidative stress parameters in children undergoing surgery.

brief_summary:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease that primarily affects the joints, causing pain, swelling, stiffness, and loss of function. Synovial fibroblasts play a key role in RA pathogenesis, with treatment-refractory patients demonstrating increased numbers of these cells. The goal of this study is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of ABBV-2294 (a combination of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib) compared to each drug alone in treating moderately to severely active RA. The platform study will measure improvements in disease activity using the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria, changes in disease activity scores, and quality of life measures.

ABBV-2294 is an investigational combination drug being developed for the treatment of moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis. This is a Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind platform study. In sub-study 1, participants are placed in 1 of 5 groups, called treatment arms. Each group receives a different treatment consisting of either ABBV-722 alone, upadacitinib alone, or various doses of ABBV-722 combined with upadacitinib. Adult participants with a diagnosis of moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have failed at least 1 prior biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (bDMARD) will be enrolled. Around 250 participants will be enrolled in the study at multiple sites worldwide.

Participants will receive oral tablet doses of ABBV-2294 (combination of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib), ABBV-722 alone, or upadacitinib alone. The study comprises a 24-week Double-Blind Phase (Period 1) followed by an optional 52-week Blinded Long Term Extension Phase (Period 2), for a total treatment duration of up to 76 weeks. After completing treatment, participants will have a 30-day Follow-Up Period.

There may be higher treatment burden for participants in this trial compared to their standard of care due to study procedures. Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a hospital or clinic, including screening, baseline, and scheduled visits through Week 76, followed by a follow-up visit. The effects of the treatment will be checked by medical assessments, blood tests, checking for side effects, and completing questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving ACR50 Response
Number of Participants Experiencing Adverse Events
title: Platform Study of Targeted Therapies for Adults With Moderately to Severely Active Rheumatoid Arthritis

brief_summary:
Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that affects the tissues supporting the teeth and can lead to progressive tissue destruction. Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disease characterized by persistently elevated blood glucose levels. These two conditions are closely related, and genetic factors may influence their development and severity.

This observational study aims to evaluate the distribution of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) and DNA methyltransferase 3B (DNMT3B) gene polymorphisms in healthy individuals, individuals with periodontitis, individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus, and individuals with both conditions. The study also aims to investigate the associations between these genetic variations and periodontal clinical parameters.

The study includes 200 participants divided into four groups of 50 individuals each: healthy individuals, individuals with type 2 diabetes without periodontitis, individuals with periodontitis without type 2 diabetes, and individuals with both type 2 diabetes and periodontitis.

Periodontal examinations include the assessment of plaque index, gingival index, probing pocket depth, clinical attachment loss, and gingival recession. Venous blood samples are collected for molecular analysis of MTHFR and DNMT3B gene polymorphisms.

The findings may contribute to a better understanding of the potential role of genetic factors in periodontal disease and its relationship with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
interventions: MTHFR and DNMT3B Genetic Polymorphism Analysis
primary_outcomes: MTHFR C677T (rs1801133) Genotype Distribution
MTHFR A1298C (rs1801131) Genotype Distribution
DNMT3B -149C>T (rs2424913) Genotype Distribution
title: Evaluation of MTHFR and DNMT3B Gene Polymorphisms Along With Periodontal Clinical Parameters in Healthy Individuals and Individuals With Type 2 Diabetes and Periodontitis

brief_summary:
The BRAVO study (Bundibugyo: Respondre Avec la Vaccination, "On est ensemble") was developed in response to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The study focuses on frontline workers (FLWs), who are at increased risk of infection because of their involvement in patient care, outbreak response activities, and contact with affected communities. Protecting this population is critical for maintaining healthcare services and strengthening outbreak control efforts.

Currently, there is no licensed vaccine specifically targeting Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) for broad use. However, ERVEBO®, a vaccine licensed against Zaire ebolavirus, is available and has demonstrated a favorable safety profile. Although preclinical and immunological evidence suggests that ERVEBO® may provide some degree of cross-protection against BDBV, the extent of protection remains uncertain. BRAVO therefore aims both to support rapid vaccination of frontline workers during the outbreak and to generate evidence that can inform future vaccine policy and preparedness strategies.

BRAVO is designed as a phased study embedded within the public health response. The study population includes adults aged 18 years and older working in Ebola treatment centers, healthcare facilities, or community-based outbreak response activities in affected areas. Both clinical and non-clinical personnel may participate if their duties place them at risk of exposure to infected individuals, infectious materials, or affected communities.

The study consists of three steps:

Step A: Immediate deployment and evaluation of ERVEBO® during the outbreak. Step B: Potential future evaluation of heterologous prime-boost vaccination strategies if additional vaccines become available and remain relevant.

Step C: Potential contribution to evaluation of future Bundibugyo virus-specific vaccines.

The primary focus of the current study is Step A, which is a prospective cohort study conducted under real-world outbreak conditions. The main objective is to assess the effectiveness of ERVEBO® vaccination against Bundibugyo virus disease, severe disease outcomes, and death. The primary effectiveness endpoint is whether vaccination reduces case fatality among laboratory-confirmed BVD cases hospitalized in Ebola treatment facilities.

Secondary objectives include evaluating whether vaccination reduces:

BVD-related mortality in the cohort, Incidence of symptomatic laboratory-confirmed BVD, Indicators of severe disease among confirmed cases.

Safety is also an important component of the study. Serious adverse events occurring within one month after vaccination will be documented, and pregnancy outcomes among enrolled pregnant participants will be monitored.

Participants may be enrolled regardless of vaccination status, allowing comparisons between vaccinated and unvaccinated frontline workers as vaccine deployment progresses according to operational feasibility and risk prioritization. Written informed consent will be obtained before enrollment and vaccination. The consent process will clearly communicate that protection against Bundibugyo virus has not been established and that additional vaccine options may become available in the future.

Participants will generally be followed for six months after enrollment, or until the end of the outbreak if it occurs earlier. Pregnant participants will be followed through pregnancy outcomes. An additional component within Ebola treatment centers will collect information on frontline workers presenting with symptoms compatible with BVD, supporting supplementary analyses of vaccine effectiveness using routinely collected clinical and laboratory data.

Step A aims to vaccinate approximately 20,000 frontline workers during the first six months of implementation. Based on projected outbreak assumptions, the study may generate sufficient confirmed BVD cases to provide meaningful estimates of vaccine effectiveness, particularly regarding protection against death.

Beyond evaluating the immediate impact of vaccination, BRAVO is expected to strengthen outbreak preparedness by establishing systems for vaccination delivery, pharmacovigilance, data collection, and participant communication. The study is designed to provide decision-relevant evidence during the outbreak rather than after it, helping guide future recommendations for Bundibugyo virus vaccine strategies.

Enrollment and vaccination are planned from September through December 2026, with follow-up continuing through June 2027. Final analysis and reporting are expected in September 2027.
primary_outcomes: Case fatality among laboratory-confirmed BVD cases hospitalized in Ebola health facilities
title: BRAVO is a Phased Outbreak-response Study in the DRC Evaluating ERVEBO® Vaccination in ~20,000 Frontline Workers During the 2026 BDV Outbreak, Step A Assesses Real-world Effectiveness, Safety, and Impact on Severe Disease and Mortality, While Generating Evidence for Future BDV Vaccination Strategies

brief_summary:
This study will test CBT-248, an experimental medicine being developed for chronic pancreatitis. Chronic pancreatitis causes ongoing inflammation and damage to the pancreas, which can cause pain and problems with digestion and blood sugar control.

The study will involve 32 healthy adults. It will look at side effects at different doses, measure the amount of medicine in the blood over time, and examine whether taking it with food changes these amounts.

Participants will be divided into four groups of eight. In each group, six people will receive CBT-248 and two will receive a placebo, a capsule that looks like the medicine but contains no active drug. Treatment will be assigned by chance. Participants and the study staff assessing them will not know who receives CBT-248 or placebo.

Three groups will receive one dose after fasting. Participants will enter the clinic two days before dosing and may leave the day after dosing, once the required checks are complete. They will return for follow-up visits four and six days after dosing.

The fourth group will receive two doses on separate occasions: one after fasting and one after starting a high-fat, high-calorie meal. Each person will receive the same treatment, CBT-248 or placebo, on both occasions. The second dose will be given after the required safety results and measurements of medicine levels have been reviewed. Each occasion will involve a clinic stay and follow-up visits as described above.

During the study, participants will have blood tests, physical examinations, checks of blood pressure and other vital signs, and tests that record the heart's electrical activity. The study team will also ask about side effects.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with Adverse Events (AEs), as assessed by a 5-point scale, CTCAE v5.0.
title: A Phase 1 Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Food Effect of CBT-248 in Healthy Adult Participants

brief_summary:
Octogenarian patients with colorectal cancer are a growing population with substantial heterogeneity in frailty, functional reserve, nutritional status, and comorbidity. Chronological age alone does not adequately capture this variation in perioperative risk. Although geriatric assessment has been increasingly incorporated into the care of older patients with cancer, comprehensive geriatric assessment can be difficult to implement routinely in colorectal surgical practice.

The SGA-OCRC study is a prospective, multicenter observational cohort study designed to address this gap. The investigators will evaluate whether a pragmatic simplified geriatric assessment provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical, laboratory, and tumor-related risk factors in patients aged ≥80 years with non-metastatic, resectable colorectal cancer. The study will develop and internally validate a preoperative prediction model for 90-day major adverse postoperative outcomes using contemporary prediction-model methodology. Particular attention will be given to model calibration, clinical utility, and internal validation rather than predictor selection based solely on statistical significance.
conditions: Octogenarian Patients With Non-metastatic Resectable Colorectal Cancer
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: 90-day major adverse postoperative outcomes (MAPO)
title: SGA-OCRC: Prediction of 90-Day Major Adverse Postoperative Outcomes in Octogenarians With Resectable Colorectal Cancer

brief_summary: This prospective, single-center, randomized controlled, double-blind (participant and outcomes assessor) trial compares ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block (ESPB) and quadro-iliac plane block (QIPB) in adult patients undergoing elective primary unilateral total hip arthroplasty (THA) under spinal anesthesia. Eighty patients will be randomized 1:1 to receive either block in addition to a standardized multimodal analgesia protocol. The primary outcome is cumulative opioid consumption (intravenous morphine equivalents, mg) during the first 24 postoperative hours. Secondary outcomes include quality of recovery (QoR-15), pain scores, opioid consumption at later time points, quadriceps strength, mobilization, patient satisfaction, and safety outcomes. It is hypothesized that QIPB will reduce 24-hour opioid consumption more than ESPB.
primary_outcomes: Cumulative opioid consumption in the first 24 postoperative hours
title: Comparison of Ultrasound-Guided Erector Spinae Plane Block and Quadro-Iliac Plane Block in Elective Primary Unilateral Total Hip Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
Malignant phyllodes tumor of the breast is a rare fibroepithelial tumor. Patients with metastatic or unresectable disease have limited systemic treatment options, and there remains a need for biomarkers that can dynamically reflect disease changes during treatment. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) may provide additional information on tumor burden and disease progression through a minimally invasive blood-based approach.

This prospective, multicenter, observational cohort study will enroll approximately 50 patients with advanced malignant phyllodes tumors of the breast who have distant metastases or are currently not candidates for curative surgery and are planning to start systemic therapy. Peripheral blood samples will be collected before treatment and at predefined time points during the current systemic treatment line, including time points corresponding to routine imaging assessments. Individualized tumor-informed ctDNA monitoring panels will be established using patient-specific somatic variants identified from tumor whole-exome sequencing obtained during routine clinical care.

The study will primarily evaluate the relationship between dynamic changes in ctDNA during the current systemic treatment line and progression-free survival (PFS), and will explore the potential value of longitudinal ctDNA monitoring for disease monitoring and prognostic assessment in advanced malignant phyllodes tumors. Study ctDNA results will not be used independently to guide clinical treatment decisions.
conditions: Malignant Phyllodes Tumor of the Breast
lead_sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
primary_outcomes: Progression-Free Survival According to Early ctDNA Status Transition Patterns
title: Dynamic ctDNA Monitoring in Advanced Malignant Phyllodes Tumors of the Breast

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, open-label, 1:1 randomized non-inferiority trial with stratification. The study will enroll patients aged 18-60 years with FLT3-ITD-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who are in first complete remission (CR1) and have no detectable FLT3-ITD measurable residual disease (MRD) by polymerase chain reaction-next-generation sequencing (PCR-NGS) before allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT).

Eligible patients will be randomly assigned to receive either reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC) or myeloablative conditioning (MAC) before allo-HSCT. All patients will receive FLT3 inhibitor maintenance therapy after transplantation.

The primary objective is to determine whether RIC is non-inferior to MAC in terms of 2-year relapse-free survival (RFS), defined as the time from transplantation to relapse or death from any cause. Secondary objectives include comparisons of overall survival (OS), non-relapse mortality (NRM), cumulative incidence of relapse, and graft-versus-host disease (GVHD)-free, relapse-free survival (GRFS) between the two conditioning groups.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University
primary_outcomes: 2-year relapse-free survival (RFS)
title: MAC vs RIC for Transplantation in FLT3-ITD-Mutated AML Guided by UHS-NGS MRD ( FLT3 - MAC vs RIC )

brief_summary:
Premature babies, especially those who need breathing support for many days, are at risk of developing a long-term lung condition called bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). BPD usually means that the baby still needs oxygen or breathing support around 36 weeks' postmenstrual age. This condition can make recovery longer and may affect the baby's breathing and development later in life.

This study looked at whether a low dose of dexamethasone, a steroid medicine that reduces inflammation, could help premature babies who were still dependent on a ventilator or non-invasive breathing support after the first week of life. The medicine was given using the DART protocol, which is a short, low-dose course of dexamethasone designed to help babies come off breathing support while reducing the risk of side effects.

The study was conducted in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at the Children's Hospital, Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), Islamabad. A total of 93 premature babies were included. All babies were more than 7 days old, born between 28 and 36 weeks of pregnancy, weighed less than 2000 grams at birth, and still needed significant breathing support. Babies with certain serious conditions, such as major congenital abnormalities, severe intestinal disease, or previous steroid exposure, were not included.

Investigators recorded each baby's oxygen requirement and ventilator pressure before and during dexamethasone treatment. They also observed whether the baby could be successfully removed from the ventilator within 10 days, how long oxygen and breathing support were needed, and whether any side effects occurred.

After treatment, babies needed less oxygen and lower ventilator pressure. The oxygen requirement decreased from 0.56 to 0.33, and mean airway pressure decreased from 12.3 to 8.9 cmH₂O. Seventy out of 93 babies, or 75.3%, were successfully extubated within 10 days. At 36 weeks' postmenstrual age, 26.9% of babies met the criteria for BPD.

The short-term side effects were manageable. Eleven babies developed temporary high blood sugar, and six developed high blood pressure; both were treated medically. No gastrointestinal perforation or steroid-related death was observed.

This study suggests that late, low-dose dexamethasone may help selected premature babies reduce breathing support and come off the ventilator earlier. However, because this was a single-arm study without a comparison group, it cannot prove that dexamethasone prevents BPD. Larger controlled studies with long-term follow-up are needed to confirm the benefits and safety of this treatment.

brief_summary:
This study evaluates a new closed-loop rehabilitation system for stroke survivors with arm weakness. The system combines a brain-computer interface (BCI, a special cap that reads brain signals), spinal cord stimulation (a temporary implanted electrode that sends gentle electrical pulses to the spine), and a robotic hand exoskeleton. When the participant imagines moving their affected hand, the system detects this intention from brain signals and immediately triggers the spinal stimulation and robotic assistance to help complete the movement. The goal is to test whether this "brain-spine-hand" closed-loop approach is safe and can improve upper limb function after stroke.

About 30 stroke patients with chronic arm weakness will be enrolled. Participants will first undergo brain signal testing to confirm they can produce detectable movement intentions. Eligible participants will then have a temporary spinal cord stimulator electrode placed under the skin near the spine. Over the next 4 weeks, they will receive daily training sessions (about 90 minutes, 5 days per week) using the closed-loop system. After 4 weeks, the electrode will be removed, and participants will continue standard rehabilitation. Hand and arm function will be assessed before, during, and after the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) Score
title: Closed-Loop SCS-BCI for Post-Stroke Hemiplegia

brief_summary:
Background and rationale. Although the literature suggests that caregivers have different needs at various stages of the patient's illness, to date, most studies have focused only on the needs of caregivers of patients with specific diseases or during specific periods of the illness trajectory, and have not explored changes in caregivers' needs throughout the entire neuromotor recovery process, from admission to discharge in rehabilitation wards. In a patient-centered care perspective, it is important not only to explore the informal experiences of patients and caregivers regarding outcomes and consequences of the transition from hospital to home, but also their perspectives on interventions that would support them in self-management. In this context, this study represents the next phase of a qualitative study that identified the underlying dimensions of caregivers' informational needs, essential for constructing a measurement tool that allows both qualitative and quantitative assessment of these needs. The tool would make it possible to identify, upon patient admission to rehabilitation, the essential informational needs in order to address them during hospitalization. The same items would also serve to assess the response obtained, in terms of healthcare service quality, before discharge.

Study design. Experimental with low level of intervention. Objectives. The study aims to validate a questionnaire specifically developed to detect and assess the informational needs of caregivers of neurological patients during rehabilitation hospitalization (post-acute phase).

Endpoint. Creation of a reliable and valid tool for detecting the informational needs of caregivers of neurological patients during rehabilitation hospitalization.
primary_outcomes: Validation of the QBI questionnaire
title: Informational Needs of Caregivers of Patients With Neuromotor Disease in Rehabilitation Hospitalization: Validation Study of the QBI-R/V

HOPES (Hops On Psychological and Estrogenic Symptoms in Menopause) is a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled nutritional intervention study in 120 peri- and postmenopausal women aged 45 to 60 years with moderate to severe menopausal symptoms. For 12 weeks, participants take one capsule per day of either a full spectrum hop (Humulus lupulus L.) extract or a soy isoflavone extract. Both products are marketed dietary supplements, and there is no placebo arm.

The main question is whether the hop extract, which combines prenylated flavonoids with bitter acids, improves the psychological symptoms of menopause (depressive mood, irritability, anxiety, and physical and mental exhaustion) more than the soy extract. The main outcome is the change in the psychological subscale of the Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) from baseline to week 12.

Secondary outcomes include the other MRS domains, anxiety, depressive symptoms, menopause-related quality of life, body composition, and safety.

brief_summary:
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a developmental condition that can affect communication, social interaction, and behavior. Identifying ASD early helps children and families access support services sooner. Pupillometry is a way of measuring the nervous system and brain function by recording the pupil response to light. It is a non-invasive technology that may support screening practices by providing health care providers with an objective physical measure to bolster behavioral screening tools used to identify children with ASD .

This study is evaluating how well the APS Detect™ handheld pupillometer works to help screen for ASD in children 2 to 4 years of age during routine pediatric healthcare visits. This investigational device measures the child's pupil response to light and uses these measurements to estimate the likelihood of ASD.

Researchers will compare screening results using the APS Detect with the results of reference standard clinical assessments used to determine whether a child has autism. The study will assess how accurately the device identifies children with autism compared to children with typical development based on the Autism Pupil Screen (APS) score.

The study will also evaluate whether the device provides the same results when used by different healthcare professionals. Information collected during this study will be used to evaluate device performance, safety, and suitability for use in pediatric healthcare settings and may support future review by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

brief_summary:
Beta-blockers are generally prescribed for the treatment of atrial fibrillation. Their purpose is to slow the heart rate and thereby reduce the workload on the heart. However, beta-blockers can affect patients' quality of life, for example by reducing physical performance or causing fatigue in daily life.

In this study, we aim to determine whether calcium channel blockers can improve the treatment of atrial fibrillation and have a positive impact on the quality of life of patients with atrial fibrillation compared with beta-blockers. We will also investigate how calcium channel blockers affect the physical exercise capacity. In addition, we will monitor potential side effects of both medications and explore whether there are any differences between women and men over the course of the study.

Both study medications, the calcium channel blocker diltiazem and the beta-blocker bisoprolol, are approved by authorities and are recommended by the European Society of Cardiology for rate control in atrial fibrillation.

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a risk-adapted treatment strategy incorporating induction therapy (Gemcitabine + Cisplatin) with Anlotinib plus Benmelstobart, followed by treatment allocation based on post-induction plasma cell-free Epstein-Barr virus DNA (cfEBV DNA) status and radiographic response in patients with locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The primary objectives are to evaluate the post-induction therapy complete response rate in the overall study population and event-free survival in the high-risk group.

brief_summary:
This clinical study is designed to evaluate a combined treatment approach in adults with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma that has spread to the peritoneum (peritoneal metastasis), as confirmed by imaging, peritoneal fluid analysis, or laparoscopy. The study population also includes patients with malignant ascites. These patients have experienced disease progression despite receiving standard therapy. Management of this condition is particularly challenging because systemically administered chemotherapeutic agents achieve limited concentrations at peritoneal tumor sites, resulting in suboptimal disease control.

In this study, participants will receive a multi-modal treatment regimen consisting of the following components administered concurrently: (1) heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) using nab-paclitaxel (albumin-bound paclitaxel), delivered directly into the abdominal cavity via a device that maintains the perfusate temperature at 42-43°C; (2) retlirafusp alfa, a PD-L1/TGF-βRII bispecific antibody fusion protein that simultaneously blocks two signaling pathways involved in tumor proliferation and angiogenesis; (3) intravenous nab-paclitaxel; and (4) apatinib, an oral small-molecule VEGFR-2 inhibitor that suppresses tumor-driven angiogenesis. The hyperthermia is expected to enhance the cytotoxic efficacy of intraperitoneal chemotherapy against peritoneal tumor deposits, while the bispecific antibody and apatinib are intended to control extra-peritoneal disease.

The primary objective of this study is to assess the safety and efficacy of this combined regimen, with a focus on disease control and overall survival. Participants will first complete an induction treatment phase, followed by repeated treatment cycles administered approximately every three weeks, and then proceed to maintenance therapy with retlirafusp alfa alone for up to two years. Throughout the study, participants will undergo regular imaging scans, laboratory tests, and clinical evaluations to monitor tumor response, treatment-related adverse events, and quality of life. This is a single-center study conducted in China.
primary_outcomes: 1-year OS rate
title: Application of Intraperitoneal Hyperthermic Chemotherapy in the Treatment of Gastric Cancer With Peritoneal Metastasis

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and feasibility of peri-transplant gecacitinib in patients with myelofibrosis undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT).

Myelofibrosis is a bone marrow disorder that can cause reduced blood cell production, enlargement of the spleen, and other complications. Allogeneic stem cell transplantation offers a potential cure, but its benefits may be limited by graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), disease relapse, and transplant-related complications.

This is a multicenter, prospective, open-label, single-arm clinical study. Participants will receive gecacitinib before, during, and after transplantation, together with standard transplantation care and GVHD prophylaxis.

The primary objective is to evaluate GVHD-free, relapse-free survival (GRFS) at 1 year after transplantation. GRFS measures survival without severe acute GVHD, chronic GVHD requiring systemic immunosuppressive treatment, disease relapse or progression, or death.

The study plans to enroll approximately 46 participants, with 43 expected to be evaluable for the primary endpoint. Participants will be followed for up to 2 years after transplantation. Secondary assessments include overall survival, progression-free survival, GVHD, disease relapse, non-relapse mortality, hematopoietic engraftment, treatment feasibility, and safety.

primary_outcomes: 1-Year GVHD-Free, Relapse-Free Survival (GRFS)

brief_summary:
This pilot randomized controlled trial aims to examine the effect of a 6-week intergenerational interaction program, conducted between older adults living in a nursing home and nursing students, on joy of life and loneliness in older adults and on ageism in nursing students.

Older adults living in Istanbul Darülaceze will be randomly assigned to an intervention group or a control group. In the intervention group, each older adult will be paired with a nursing student, and the same pair will meet once a week for about 2 hours over 6 weeks. The pairs will jointly decide on activities such as games (e.g., backgammon, dominoes, puzzles), reading and cultural sharing, creative work (e.g., drawing, collage, life-story albums), and sharing skills and experiences. Each session will end with a structured, mutual reflection. Older adults in the control group will continue their usual daily routine and will be offered the same program after the study ends, if they wish.

Joy of life and loneliness in older adults, and ageism in nursing students, will be measured before and after the program.

brief_summary: Acute heart failure is a common and serious condition that frequently brings patients to the emergency department. Emergency physicians need quick and reliable methods to evaluate the severity of the condition and monitor the response to initial treatment. This observational study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of bedside ultrasound (Point-of-Care Ultrasound or POCUS) in predicting clinical outcomes for these patients. Researchers will perform bedside ultrasound scans on adult patients presenting with acute heart failure. The scans will be performed twice: first upon admission to the emergency department, and again three hours after starting treatment. The ultrasound protocol will check the heart's pumping ability, look for fluid in the lungs, and measure specific veins (inferior vena cava and internal jugular vein) to assess fluid overload. The main goal of this study is to see if these ultrasound measurements can successfully predict important patient outcomes, including the likelihood of returning to the hospital within 30 days and 30-day survival.

brief_summary:
The SCREENS-BP study is a randomized crossover study evaluating the effects of smartphone use and television viewing on blood pressure (BP) measurements in 96 adults.

Each participant will undergo four sets of automated BP measurements under standardized conditions. The first three sets will be performed in random order: without distractions, while actively using a smartphone, and while watching a standardized television video. A fourth set without distractions will be performed at the end. Each set will consist of a two-minute walk, five minutes of rest followed by three BP measurements taken at one-minute intervals, without staff present.

The primary outcome is the within-participant difference in systolic BP between each distraction condition and the reference BP, calculated from the mean of the two sets without distractions. Secondary outcomes include differences in diastolic BP and heart rate. Exploratory analyses will assess potential differences according to participant characteristics.

The findings will help determine whether common technological distractions influence BP measurement accuracy and inform recommendations for BP measurement in clinical, home, and research settings.

brief_summary:
Background: Obesity affects 18.1% of adults in France and leads to numerous chronic complications as well as functional limitations (fatigability, dyspnea). While Adapted Physical Activity (APA) is an essential first-line intervention, maintaining independent adherence after discharge from a rehabilitation center remains a major challenge. The use of remote medical monitoring via digital medical devices provides asynchronous, personalized, and secure follow-up to optimize this transition.

Objective: The objective of the ON-TRAC study is to demonstrate the superiority of adding the remote medical monitoring device AXOMOVE THERAPY® compared to conventional care alone in improving the cardiorespiratory and functional capacities of patients with obesity at 6 months.

Methods: In the context of this interventional, prospective, multicenter, controlled, randomized (1:1 ratio, stratified by center), single-blind clinical study, 184 patients (92 per arm) will be included over a 6-month follow-up period.

Control Group (CG) (N=92): Will receive conventional multidisciplinary care (HAS recommendations) combined with a recommendation for independent APA and the provision of a generic exercise booklet.

Interventional Group (IG) (N=92): Will receive the same conventional care, supplemented by a personalized APA program prescribed, guided, and supervised remotely via the AXOMOVE THERAPY® medical device, which includes an automatic alert system in case of pain, difficulty, or decreased adherence.

Outcomes:

The primary endpoint is the change in distance covered during the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) between inclusion (M0) and the end of follow-up (M6), evaluated in a standardized manner by blinded healthcare staff.

The secondary endpoints include:

Changes in weight, waist circumference, BMI, fat/muscle mass ratio, and the percentage of patients losing ≥ 5% of their body weight at 6 months.

Physical activity level (IPAQ-SF), pain intensity (VAS), fear of movement (TSK-17).

Impact on global and specific quality of life (QOLOD, EQ-5D-5L).

Self-confidence and anxiety/depression levels (HADS).

Adherence and use of co-interventions (APA sessions, physiotherapy).

Duration of sick leave, and the number of unscheduled consultations or hospitalizations.

Economic evaluation: overall cost of care, expenses reimbursed by the National Health Insurance (Assurance Maladie), and out-of-pocket costs for patients.

Usability, satisfaction, and safety (evaluated for IG patients only).

Timeline: The total planned duration for this study is 18 months, including 12 months of recruitment and a follow-up of 6 to 6.5 months per participant.
primary_outcomes: Distance walked in the 6-Minute Walk Test
title: Evaluation of the Axomove Therapy Medical Device to Facilitate Adapted Physical Activity for Patients With Obesity

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if applying positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) improves neurological outcome in adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest who receive an advanced airway (supraglottic airway device or endotracheal tube). The main question it aims to answer is:

Does ventilating with 8 cm H2O PEEP during CPR improve neurological outcome at hospital discharge, as measured by the utility-weighted modified Rankin Scale (UW-mRS)?

Researchers will compare an 8 cm H2O PEEP valve to a look-alike sham valve that provides no PEEP (zero end-expiratory pressure) to see if PEEP improves neurological outcome.

Participants will:

* Be ventilated during CPR with a resuscitator fitted with either the PEEP valve or the sham valve, assigned at random through pre-assembled kits. Patients, ambulance staff and researchers will not know which valve is used.
* Receive otherwise standard advanced life support
* Be asked for consent afterwards (deferred consent), with outcome data taken from routine hospital records
* Complete a quality-of-life questionnaire by telephone 6 months after the arrest, if they survive
primary_outcomes: Neurological outcomes

brief_summary: Over the past decades, the volume and complexity of gastrointestinal endoscopy (GI) interventions have increased due to the progress in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures along worldwide implementation of colorectal cancer screening and surveillance programs. Nowadays, the first line for procedural sedation is either propofol or midazolam, in combination with opiates when analgesia is required, depending on the country's human resources, service framework, and legislation. Provision of sedation has been shown to decrease patient's anxiety, discomfort and pain improving at the same time procedure efficiency. However, administration of sedative and/or analgesic medications is not risk-free, as a variety of serious adverse effects i.e. respiratory depression, arrhythmia or hypotension may occur. In this regard, optimal discharge management after a procedure with sedation/analgesia, until the patient returns to a fully conscious, clinically stable, and ideally cognitively functional state can be challenging for both endoscopists and nursing personnel\[6\]. In an effort to address this, international endoscopy societies suggest the use of standardized discharge criteria and scoring systems such as the Post Anesthesia Recovery (PAR), or Aldrete, score, Aldrete scoring system and the modified post-anesthesia discharge scoring system (mPADSS), combined with clinical assessment to ensure patient safe discharge and readiness for discharge. Still, data supporting the use of Aldrete score derive mainly from studies evaluating patients discharge post-surgery, while evidence for model use in the setting of GI endoscopic procedures remain scant\[8,9\]. In this context, the investigators conducted a randomized controlled trial (RCT) aiming to explore the impact of Aldrete scoring system on safe discharge of participants who have undergone GI procedures under analgesia/sedation.
interventions: The post-anesthesia recovery or Aldrete score has been commonly used to clinically assess the physical status of patients recovering from the anesthetic experience and to follow their awakening proces

primary_outcomes: Recovery time
title: Recovery Time With the Application of ALDRETE Score in Patients Undergoing Gastrointestinal Endoscopy

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn whether a new oral nutritional supplement is acceptable to adults who are malnourished, or at risk of malnutrition, and need nutritional support.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do participants tolerate the supplement without stomach or bowel problems?
* How much of the prescribed supplement do participants take each day?
* How do participants rate the taste, texture and overall experience of taking the supplement?

Researchers will also record any side effects.

Participants will:

* Take the supplement every day for 7 days, as prescribed by their dietitian
* Keep a daily diary of how much they take and any stomach or bowel symptoms

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial aims to evaluate and compare the clinical and radiographic performance of 38% silver diamine fluoride (SDF) with 38% silver diamine fluoride followed by light curing in children with carious primary molars.

Children aged 4-8 years with active caries in mandibular primary molars will be included in the study. One group will receive 38% silver diamine fluoride followed by LED light curing, while the comparison group will receive 38% silver diamine fluoride without light curing.

The primary outcome is postoperative pain, assessed using the visual analogue scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes include caries lesion arrest, lesion extension and severity, signs of infection, pain on percussion, pathological tooth mobility, and radiographic changes.

Participants will be followed for 12 months. The findings may help determine whether adding light curing to silver diamine fluoride application improves the management of caries in primary molars.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative pain
title: Clinical and Radiographic Evaluation of Silver Diamine Fluoride Versus Light-Cured Silver Diamine Fluoride in Carious Primary Molars

brief_summary:

The primary objective is to evaluate changes in corneal curvature, measured by steep keratometry (K2), maximum keratometry (Kmax), and mean keratometry (Kmean), from preoperative baseline to six months following CTAK.

Secondary outcomes include changes in uncorrected and corrected distance visual acuity, refractive stability, documented postoperative complications, subsequent corneal transplantation, and exploratory analyses across payer categories.

The study uses existing medical records from up to eight participating clinical sites, targeting up to 100 treated eyes. No study-specific intervention, patient contact, or prospective clinical assessments will occur.

brief_summary:
This study aims to develop a valid and reliable assessment scale for evaluating body hygiene status in bedbound individuals. Maintaining body hygiene is an essential component of nursing care, particularly for patients who depend on others for daily activities.

The study is designed as a methodological study involving sequential qualitative and quantitative phases. Initially, semi-structured interviews will be conducted with intensive care nurses experienced in providing hygiene care to bedbound patients. The findings, together with relevant literature, will inform the development of an initial item pool.

Following item development and preliminary evaluation, the draft scale will be tested in at least 100 bedbound patients. Further psychometric evaluation will be conducted using a sample size determined according to the final number of scale items.

Body hygiene status will be assessed through observation during routine nursing care. No experimental treatment, invasive procedure, or additional medical intervention will be performed. The study aims to provide a standardized instrument to support the assessment of body hygiene status in bedbound individuals.
conditions: Body Hygiene Status in Bedbound Individuals
primary_outcomes: Construct Validity of the Body Hygiene Status Assessment Scale
title: Development of a Body Hygiene Assessment Scale for Bedbound Individuals

brief_summary: Adhesive capsulitis (also known as frozen shoulder) causes pain and stiffness in the joint. It can interfere with such ordinary activities as dressing, reaching up to a shelf and lying on the affected side at night and may last for months . Manual therapy is a typical treatment component, but it remains unclear to clinicians which technique is most effective . The two hands-on techniques, the Spencer technique and the Ola Grimsby techniques will be compared in a randomized clinical trial of both techniques combined with the scapular motor training programme. Idiopathic adhesive capsulitis patients will be randomly assigned to either of two treatments groups and undergo treatment three times weekly for six weeks. Baseline and after last session pain, shoulder range of motion and disability will be recorded. The goal is to determine if one technique is more effective than the other (when it is trained concurrently with it) when training scapular control.

brief_summary: Early childhood is a critical period for the development of emotional competencies that contribute to children's psychosocial well-being and adaptive functioning. This study aimed to examine the effects of a preventive emotion-focused intervention on emotion recognition and life skills in preschool children. A pilot cluster-randomized controlled pretest-posttest design was used with 62 children aged 48-79 months in a kindergarten in Central Anatolia, Türkiye. Four classrooms were randomized within two age groups, with one intervention and one control classroom in each age group. The intervention comprised six weeks of emotion-focused activities involving drama, music, art, play, and storytelling. Emotion recognition and life skills were assessed before and after the intervention using Denham's Affect Knowledge Test and the Early Childhood Life Skills Scale, respectively.

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the effects of pA1c®HI, a heat-inactivated postbiotic derived from the bacterium Pediococcus acidilactici, on blood glucose regulation and other aspects of metabolic health in adults with elevated blood glucose levels who do not have diagnosed diabetes.

The study will include approximately 100 adults aged 18 to 80 years with glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels of 5.7% to less than 6.5%, a range consistent with prediabetes. A postbiotic is a preparation of inactivated microorganisms and/or their components that may provide health benefits. pA1c®HI does not contain live bacteria.

This is an open-label, single-group study. All participants will take one capsule of pA1c®HI daily for 12 weeks. There is no placebo or separate control group. Researchers will compare measurements taken before and after the intervention to assess changes over time. Participants will continue their usual medical care and previously established lifestyle recommendations.

The study will include assessments at the beginning and end of the intervention. These will include blood tests, measurements of body weight and other physical characteristics, questionnaires, and continuous glucose monitoring for 14 days at each assessment period. Participants will also provide stool samples for analysis of gut microbiota composition. Blood tests will assess glycated hemoglobin, fasting glucose, insulin-related markers, blood lipids, liver function, and other parameters. Researchers will also measure glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), a hormone involved in blood glucose regulation, including its response to a mixed meal.

The main objective is to evaluate changes in HbA1c after 12 weeks of daily pA1c®HI supplementation. Other objectives include assessing changes in glucose levels and variability, insulin resistance markers, blood lipids, GLP-1 responses, gut microbiota composition, and body measurements. The study will also assess adherence to supplementation and monitor safety and tolerability.

The findings will help researchers understand the potential effects of pA1c®HI on metabolic health in adults with elevated blood glucose levels. Because the study does not include a placebo or control group, changes observed during the study cannot be attributed to the postbiotic with the same certainty as in a controlled trial.
primary_outcomes: Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c)
title: Efficacy of the pA1c®HI Postbiotic in Metabolic Regulation in Healthy Individuals With Hyperglycemia

brief_summary: In this four-arm randomized controlled clinical trial, 120 adults aged 18-50 years with baseline Modified Dental Anxiety Scale scores ≥13 were allocated equally to 432 Hz-based instrumental music, water sounds, human-vocal music, or a no-audio control during standardized restorative cavity preparation. Heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, peripheral oxygen saturation, and body temperature were recorded before and immediately after preparation; patient satisfaction was assessed after restoration. Physiological outcomes were compared using baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance, with Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons. The null hypothesis was that there would be no significant differences among the four study groups in changes in physiological parameters or post-treatment patient satisfaction. The alternative hypothesis was that at least one auditory intervention condition would differ from the other study conditions in physiological responses and/or patient satisfaction.
primary_outcomes: Change in Dental Anxiety Status and Patient Satisfaction
title: Effects of Different 432 Hz Auditory Stimuli on Physiological Stress Responses and Patient Satisfaction in Adults With Dental Anxiety During Restorative Treatment

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether two nursing interventions, lower abdominal massage and range-of-motion (ROM) exercises (gentle movements of the arm and leg joints), affect the healing of pressure injuries (bed sores) in intensive care patients who are fed through a tube (enteral nutrition).

Intensive care patients often stay in bed for long periods and are at high risk of pressure injuries. Adequate nutrition is important for wound healing, but tube-fed patients often have digestive problems such as constipation, vomiting, bloating, or food remaining in the stomach, which can interrupt feeding.

The main question this study will address is: Compared with routine care, do lower abdominal massage or ROM exercises affect digestive tolerance, nutritional markers, and pressure injury healing in tube-fed intensive care patients? The researchers hypothesize that lower abdominal massage may reduce digestive problems and support uninterrupted feeding, and that ROM exercises may support circulation and tissue healing. Both effects may, in turn, support pressure injury healing.

Adult patients who have a pressure injury and receive enteral nutrition in the intensive care units of a state hospital in Türkiye will be randomly assigned to one of three groups:

* Group 1: lower abdominal massage in addition to routine care
* Group 2: ROM exercises in addition to routine care
* Control group: routine care only The interventions will be applied for 15 minutes once a day for 7 days. Digestive tolerance (bowel movements, gastric residual volume, nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension), serum albumin, and pressure injury healing (Pressure Ulcer Scale for Healing, PUSH) will be monitored daily.

Detailed Description This is a three-arm, parallel-group, randomized controlled experimental study planned for the intensive care units of a secondary-level state hospital in Türkiye. Patients who meet the eligibility criteria will be allocated to lower abdominal massage, ROM exercise, or routine care using a computer-generated randomization list (Microsoft Excel). The sample size will be calculated with G\*Power before data collection (planned minimum: 90 patients; effect size 0.20, alpha 0.05, 95% confidence level).

Interventions: Lower abdominal massage (15 minutes: superficial effleurage, palm petrissage, fingertip vibration, closing effleurage; clockwise along the colon, with hands warmed in liquid paraffin) will be performed by an intensive care nurse. ROM exercises (flexion-extension, abduction-adduction and rotation of the upper and lower limb joints, with the patient supine; 3 repetitions per movement, held 30 seconds at the point of resistance; 15 minutes in total) will be performed after the researchers receive ROM training from a physiotherapist. The control group will receive routine intensive care only (nasogastric tube position checks, monitoring of gastric residual volume, defecation, nausea and vomiting, daily Braden Scale assessment, two-hourly repositioning, and stage-appropriate topical wound care).

Data will be collected daily at 10:00 using a Patient Information Form and an Intervention/Control Group Patient Monitoring Form. Gastric residual volume will be assessed between 02:00 and 04:00 when feeding is paused.

Planned analysis: Normality will be assessed with skewness and kurtosis values (±3). Between-group comparisons will use chi-square/Fisher's exact test, one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc tests. Within-group changes over time will use repeated-measures ANOVA, Friedman test, or Cochran's Q test as appropriate (significance p\<0.05).
conditions: Enteral Nutrition Intolerance in Critically Ill Patients
interventions: Intervention and control-group data were collected daily at 10:00 AM. In the intervention groups, each 15-minute session was followed by outcome measurements the next day before the following session,
primary_outcomes: Change in total score on the Pressure Ulcer Scale for Healing (PUSH) of the first (largest) pressure injury

brief_summary: Non-small cell lung cancer frequently spreads to the brain, and brain metastases are associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment response. This retrospective study will investigate whether quantitative features extracted from brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), known as radiomic features, are associated with the immune characteristics of brain metastases assessed by bulk RNA sequencing. The main objective is to identify relationships between MRI-based radiomic signatures and tumor immune profiles. A secondary objective is to determine whether radiomic, transcriptomic, or combined radio-transcriptomic signatures can help predict cerebral progression during immunotherapy. The study hypothesis is that MRI-based radiomic signatures may reflect the immune environment of brain metastases and could provide a non-invasive approach for predicting treatment response.

brief_summary:
Sleeve gastrectomy is the most commonly performed metabolic bariatric operation. After the operation, the upper part of the gastric sleeve can slide up through the opening in the diaphragm into the chest. This is called intrathoracic sleeve migration and is a form of sliding hiatal hernia. It may cause new reflux symptoms such as heartburn, regurgitation and vomiting, and may lead to further surgery. How often it happens is uncertain, because studies have used different definitions and tests.

This single-centre observational study included adults who had a laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy at Cairo University Hospitals between July 2024 and August 2025 and were at least one year after surgery. Each patient had a CT scan of the chest and abdomen with oral contrast to look for migration of the sleeve above the diaphragm, and completed the GERD-Q reflux questionnaire. The study measured how often intrathoracic sleeve migration occurs one year or more after sleeve gastrectomy, whether it is associated with new (de novo) reflux disease, and which patient factors may be associated with it.
interventions: CT of the thorax and abdomen with oral water-soluble contrast
primary_outcomes: Incidence of intrathoracic sleeve migration (ITSM)

brief_summary:
The growth and organization of the cerebral cortex is ensured by the oligodendrocyte-rich subplate, whose proper development depends on both subcortical structures and sensory experiences. In the incubator, the premature baby is exposed to inappropriate stimuli at a critical period of physiological immaturity and brain development. Analysis of the pathophysiological basis of neurological and behavioral disorders in premature infants highlights the interplay between biological vulnerability (cerebral alteration) and environmental factors (stress, perinatal pain and loss of emotional connection with the mother).

Developmental care aims to modify the environment in order to limit deviant developmental trajectories and reduce neurobehavioral impact, by relying on brain plasticity. This care consists of a set of environmental and behavioral strategies based on principles of balance between different stimuli adapted to cerebral maturation. The usefulness of multimodal sensory interventions as early as 28 weeks of amenorrhea has been demonstrated to offset the harmful effects of incubator dystimulation.

These interventions improve neurobehavioral disorders and reduce parental stress, but none has been shown to be superior. Welch's studies published in 2015 and 2017, based on the definition of emotional co-regulation processes, show the value of involving parents in care during hospitalization, from the incubator period onwards.

The hypothesis of this study is that multisensory intervention in a calming cycle can induce neurobehavioral improvement at term age in the very premature baby. The intervention consists of a parenting workshop and an incubator-based multisensory solicitation program with tactile, vestibular, visual and vocal contact performed by the mother or, where appropriate, the father, combined with the diffusion of maternal odor. The aim is to evaluate the effectiveness of this multisensory intervention on the behavior at term (in corrected age) of the very premature baby born between 24 and 32 weeks of amenorrhea.
primary_outcomes: Assessment of preterm behavior using the NICU Network Neurobehavioral Scale (NNNS) neurobehavioral scale
title: Effects of a Multisensory Intervention Program on the Term Behavior of the Very Premature Baby

brief_summary:

Breast sensation, including sensation of the nipple-areolar complex, may be diminished or lost following mastectomy because of injury to the sensory nerves supplying the breast skin and nipple-areolar complex. Sensory nerve coaptation may improve sensory recovery after surgery. This study will compare sensory recovery between patients who undergo sensory nerve coaptation and those who do not, with the aim of evaluating whether sensory nerve coaptation improves postoperative breast sensation.

GDC-0077 is an oral, highly selective PI3Kα inhibitor. Preclinical data from this research group showed that PI3Kα inhibition increased secondary and antral follicle counts in aged mice and promoted follicle development in cultured mouse ovaries. Twelve participants with POI will receive GDC-0077 9 mg orally three times weekly (Monday, Wednesday, Friday) for 3 weeks. The primary safety focus includes hyperglycemia, stomatitis/mucositis, and diarrhea. Ovarian function will be assessed by change in antral follicle count (AFC) from baseline at 3 months after treatment initiation, along with FSH, AMH, ovarian volume, and return of spontaneous menses.
