brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective, multicenter observational study is to learn which antibiotic treatment strategies are associated with better outcomes in critically ill adults with severe infections caused by carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB). The study will also evaluate the safety and costs of different treatments and develop prediction models to support personalized treatment decisions.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Are there differences in 28-day survival between patients receiving polymyxin-based and non-polymyxin-based antibiotic treatments?

Which treatment strategies are associated with better clinical recovery, bacterial clearance, and fewer adverse events, particularly acute kidney injury?

Can clinical data and machine learning help predict treatment outcomes and support safer, more effective treatment decisions?

Researchers will compare patients receiving polymyxin-based combination therapy with those receiving non-polymyxin-based treatments, including high-dose sulbactam-based, tigecycline-based, and newer antibiotic regimens. Treatment decisions will be made by the patients' treating physicians as part of routine clinical care, rather than assigned by the researchers.

Participants will:

Receive antibiotic treatments determined by their treating physicians.

Have clinical information collected during hospitalization, including laboratory tests, bacterial cultures, organ function, antibiotic use, adverse events, and medical costs.

Be followed for 28 days after starting targeted antibiotic treatment to assess survival and clinical outcomes.

Be contacted by telephone if necessary to confirm their health status after hospital discharge.
primary_outcomes: 28-Day All-Cause Mortality Rate
title: Targeted Antimicrobial Comparison for Treatment Individualization in Critically Ill Patients With CRAB Infection

brief_summary: A multi-Center, prospective, observational study of the disease burden of Hypophosphatasia (HPP) patients in China. brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) was to assess the feasibility, acceptability, and impacts of a whole-food plant-based (WFPB) vegan diet intervention for undergraduate university students randomly assigned, stratifying by sex and race/ethnicity, to one of two intervention groups (each with a distinct teaching-learning design, i.e., interactive (IA) versus lecture-based (LB)) and a control group. The main questions the researchers aimed to answer were:

* Were the study procedures feasible and acceptable for the overall sample and were the intervention sessions, following a WFPB vegan diet, and the prospect of continuing this diet feasible and acceptable for the intervention participants?
* Were there greater improvements in diet quality, WFPB vegan diet adherence, physical and mental health, and intrapersonal factor outcomes for the intervention group engaging in interactive learning compared to the intervention group learning through traditional lecture? And were there greater improvements in these outcomes for both intervention groups compared with the control group?

The researchers compared the group outcome means for the two intervention groups against one another and those for the two intervention groups against those of the control group.

Study participants completed two sets of measurements over the course of 6 weeks.

* All participants completed online baseline and post-intervention surveys and in-person baseline and post-intervention biometric measurements.
* Only the intervention group participants attended three 75-minute consecutive weekly intervention sessions to learn about different aspects of the WFPB vegan diet between the two sets of survey and biometric measurements.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility and Acceptability: Study Uptake
Feasibility and Acceptability: Study Attrition
Feasibility and Acceptability: Intervention Engagement
Feasibility and Acceptability: Qualitative Assessment
Feasibility and Acceptability: Food Acceptability Questionnaire
title: Testing the Feasibility and Impact of a Whole-Food Plant-Based Diet Intervention on College Students

brief_summary:
The purpose of this randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study was to investigate the acute effects of arugula extract (AE) supplementation on blood pressure, endothelial function, and circulating nitric oxide (NO) metabolites in individuals with elevated to stage 1 hypertension. Hypertension is a major contributing factor to cardiovascular disease (CVD) and is commonly associated with endothelial dysfunction and impaired NO bioavailability. Dietary nitrate supplementation has demonstrated beneficial effects on cardiovascular health through the nitrate-nitrite-NO pathway. Although nitrate-rich supplements such as beetroot juice have been extensively investigated, limited research has examined the vascular effects of arugula extract in individuals with hypertension.

Sixteen adults between the ages of 18 and 50 years with elevated to stage 1 hypertension participated in the study. Participants completed two experimental conditions in randomized order: 4,000 mg of arugula extract, providing approximately 400 mg of dietary nitrate, and 4,000 mg of psyllium husk placebo. Each condition was separated by a minimum 72-hour washout period to minimize potential carryover effects.

During each experimental condition, participants underwent baseline cardiovascular and vascular assessments before consuming the assigned supplement. Systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, and venous blood samples were collected at baseline and 1, 2, 3, and 24 hours following supplementation. Endothelial function was assessed through brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD) at baseline, 3 hours, and 24 hours post-supplementation. Blood samples were analyzed to assess circulating nitrate, nitrite, and total NO metabolites.

The primary objective was to determine whether acute arugula extract supplementation improved endothelial function and reduced blood pressure compared with placebo. Secondary objectives included evaluating changes in circulating NO metabolites. This investigation sought to determine the potential of arugula extract as a dietary nitrate intervention for improving vascular health in individuals with elevated blood pressure.
primary_outcomes: Endothelial Function
Blood Pressure
Biomarker of Nitric Oxide
Heart Rate
title: Under Pressure: Arugula Extract's Effect on Blood Pressure in Hypertensive Individuals

The primary objectives are to assess the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic profile of VT-101 and to identify a recommended dose for further study. Secondary and exploratory objectives include evaluation of preliminary antitumor activity and characterization of treatment-related effects in participants with limited standard treatment options.

brief_summary:
Immune-related ocular surface diseases are a kind of non-infectious eye disease pedigree, which is mediated by abnormal immune system function and characterized by ocular surface tissue damage. It mainly covers immune keratitis, immune disease-related dry eye, allergic keratoconjunctivitis, Thygeson superficial punctate keratitis, mucosal pemphigoid-related ocular surface damage and other clinical types, and its incidence is closely related to autoimmune disorder, abnormal immune response after infection, genetic susceptibility and environmental triggering factors.

At present, there are still obvious therapeutic limitations in clinical routine treatment for immune-related ocular surface diseases. The first-line treatment plan mainly focuses on local glucocorticoid and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs to inhibit inflammatory reaction. Although it can quickly control corneal edema and infiltration in acute stage, there are serious adverse reactions such as elevated intraocular pressure, cataract and corneal thinning and perforation after long-term use, which cannot meet the needs of long-term maintenance treatment.

Umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (UCMSC) have unique immunomodulatory characteristics in inflammatory environment. Its mechanism of action is mainly to inhibit the over-activation of immune cells and reduce the content of pro-inflammatory factors by secreting soluble cytokines and regulating the release of various anti-inflammatory factors. However, under the traditional medication mode, UCMSC can not stay on the ocular surface. Our company has developed a medicine, namely MSCohi-O lens, which uses soft hydrophilic contact lens to load UCMSC, so as to realize long-term local administration on the ocular surface, make UCMSC play an immunomodulatory role locally, inhibit the over-activation of immune/inflammatory reaction, and finally treat or alleviate the symptoms of immune-related ocular surface diseases.

This clinical study is expected to explore the clinical effect of MSCohi-O lens in the treatment of immune-related ocular surface diseases, and initially determine the clinical application of MSCohi-O lens in the treatment of immune-related ocular surface diseases, so as to provide new clinical schemes and treatment ideas for the treatment of immune-related ocular surface diseases.
primary_outcomes: The incidence and severity of adverse events within 29 days after the first administration were calculated.
title: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Safety and Effectiveness of MSCohi-O Lens in the Treatment of Immune-related Ocular Surface Diseases.

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate how closely two approaches to assessing pain-related characteristics agree in adults with chronic cervical myofascial pain syndrome (chronic neck pain associated with painful muscle trigger points).

The Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) is a questionnaire that assesses symptoms associated with increased pain sensitivity. The International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) has developed clinical criteria to identify nociplastic pain, a type of pain that cannot be fully explained by tissue damage or nerve injury. These approaches provide different types of information, and it is unclear how often they classify patients with chronic cervical myofascial pain in the same way.

This observational, cross-sectional study will include 150 adults aged 18 years or older with chronic cervical myofascial pain syndrome.

Participants will undergo a clinical assessment based on the IASP nociplastic pain criteria and complete the CSI, Neck Disability Index (NDI), and Revised Illness Perception Questionnaire (IPQ-R). Pain severity and relevant clinical information will also be recorded.

The main objective is to determine the agreement between CSI classification using a cutoff score of 40 and IASP clinical classification of nociplastic pain.

The study will also examine how often the two approaches produce different classifications and whether patients with matching or differing classifications report different emotional responses to their illness.

All assessments will be completed during a single visit. No experimental treatments or additional invasive procedures will be performed.
primary_outcomes: Agreement Between CSI and IASP Nociplastic Pain Classifications
title: Agreement Between CSI and IASP Pain Classification in Chronic Cervical Myofascial Pain

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if an online written imagery rescripting program (W-ImRs) can reduce shame and negative beliefs about oneself in Malaysian adults aged 18 to 58 who experienced childhood emotional neglect.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does W-ImRs lower shame more than psychoeducation alone?
2. Does W-ImRs lower negative beliefs about oneself more than psychoeducation alone?
3. Do more people who receive W-ImRs show reliable and meaningful improvement than people who receive psychoeducation alone?

Researcher will compare W-ImRs to a single psychoeducation session to see if W-ImRs reduces shame and negative self-beliefs. Participants in the psychoeducation group will be offered W-ImRs after the study.

Participants will:

1. Complete online questionnaires before and after the program
2. Attend a live online psychoeducation session (about 60 minutes)
3. If in the W-ImRs group, complete two written tasks about a painful childhood memory over about 4 weeks, receive written feedback from the therapist after each task, and attend a live online debriefing session (about 60 minutes)
conditions: Adult Survivors of Child Adverse Events
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Shame on the External and Internal Shame Scale (EISS) at Post-Intervention
title: Online Written Imagery Rescripting for Shame and Negative Self-Cognitions in Malaysian Adults With Childhood Emotional Neglect

brief_summary:
Study Objective: Neurosyphilis remains a major clinical challenge: despite standard first-line therapy with intravenous penicillin G, as recommended by international and Chinese guidelines, approximately 30% of patients have residual neurological impairment. Minocycline, a tetracycline antibiotic, has both anti-Treponema pallidum activity and independent anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects. We therefore designed a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate whether the addition of minocycline to penicillin, as compared with penicillin monotherapy, improves the 6-month rate of favorable neurological outcomes in patients with neurosyphilis. This trial will provide evidence-based evidence for the treatment of neurosyphilis. Inclusion Criteria: 1）Age 18-80 years; 2）Diagnosis of neurosyphilis according to the Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Syphilis, Gonorrhea and Genital Chlamydia trachomatis Infection (2020); 3）Cognitive impairment (MMSE score 10-26) or ischemic stroke-like episodes (time from onset to randomization ≤14 days, NIHSS score 1-20); 4）Written informed consent provided by the patient or their legally authorized representative. Intervention: Participants will be randomly assigned ( by chance ) to one of two groups. Group 1 will receive standard intravenous penicillin therapy plus oral minocycline for 28 days. Group 2 will receive standard intravenous penicillin therapy plus oral placebo for 28 days. All participants will receive standard penicillin treatment. Participants and their doctors will not know which group they are in. Follow-up: Participants will be followed for up to 12 months, with five follow-up visits: baseline (before treatment initiation), end of intravenous penicillin treatment (Day 12 ± 2 days), end of minocycline treatment (Day 28 + 2 days), 6 months post-treatment (Month 6 ± 7 days), and 12 months post-treatment (Month 12 ± 7 days). Assessments will include standardized neurological function scales for favorable neurological outcomes, cognitive function, neurological deficits, and activities of daily living; cerebrospinal fluid and serum efficacy marker testing; and brain MRI.

Potential Benefits and Risks: Participants may or may not benefit from participating in this study. All participants will receive standard treatment for neurosyphilis. The main risks are complications that may occur during study procedures (such as lumbar puncture, or allergic reactions to penicillin) and possible side effects of minocycline, including dizziness, vestibular side effects, nausea, or skin sensitivity to sunlight. The study team will closely monitor participants for any adverse reactions. Importance of This Study: If minocycline does help improve neurological outcomes, it could become a new treatment option for patients with neurosyphilis, thereby helping to reduce the occurrence of neurological sequelae. The implementation of this study will provide evidence-based evidence for the treatment of neurosyphilis.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants with favorable neurological outcomes at 6 months
title: Efficacy and Safety of Minocycline Add-on in Patients With Neurosyphilis

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether children and adolescents with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) who have had inactive disease for a long time can safely discontinue treatment with a tumour necrosis factor inhibitor (TNF-inhibitor) monotherapy. The trial compares TNFi withdrawal with continued treatment at a stable dose. The main question it aims to answer is whether TNF-inhibitor withdrawal increases the risk of disease flare during 12 months of follow-up compared with continued treatment. The trial will also assess time to flare, time to regain inactive disease after a flare, changes in disease activity, and the overall safety of both treatment strategies during the same period. Ninety patients aged 2 to 17 years with non-systemic JIA will take part. All of them will have had inactive disease for at least 12 months while on TNF-inhibitor monotherapy with adalimumab, etanercept or golimumab. Participants will be randomly assigned either to continue their current TNF-inhibitor treatment at a stable dose or to TNF-inhibitor withdrawal. They will be followed for 12 months at three hospitals in Norway, with regular visits where disease activity is assessed through joint examination and the Juvenile Arthritis Disease Activity Score (JADAS-27), and where side effects and other health problems are recorded. A flare is defined as a clinically significant increase in disease activity together with at least one active joint, or as agreement between the treating physician and the participant or parents that a flare has occurred.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of disease flare
title: Withdrawal Versus Continued TNF Inhibitor Monotherapy Treatment in Children With Inactive Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis

brief_summary:
This prospective observational cohort study examines whether blood pressure variability and nighttime blood pressure patterns, measured non-invasively over 72 hours with a cuffless ring-type wearable device, help predict recovery in patients with acute ischemic stroke.

In acute ischemic stroke, how much blood pressure fluctuates - and whether it drops normally during sleep - may affect brain injury and outcome. Standard cuff monitors measure blood pressure only intermittently and can disturb sleep, which limits assessment of these patterns. This study uses a finger-worn cuffless continuous monitor to capture blood pressure without disturbing sleep.

The study also examines whether the burden of pre-existing cerebral small vessel disease, seen as white matter changes on brain MRI, changes how strongly blood pressure variability relates to outcome.

Blood pressure data are collected for research analysis only and are not used to guide treatment. All clinical care follows standard stroke guidelines, regardless of study participation. The main outcome is functional recovery (modified Rankin Scale) at hospital discharge.
interventions: Cuffless ring-type continuous blood pressure monitor
primary_outcomes: Poor functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale 3-6) at discharge
title: Continuous Blood Pressure Variability and Small Vessel Disease in Acute Ischemic Stroke

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether suzetrigine (Journavx®), when added to standard multimodal pain management, can reduce opioid use while providing adequate pain control in adults undergoing surgery for an acute hip fracture. The study will enroll adults aged 18 years or older with femoral neck, intertrochanteric, pertrochanteric, or subtrochanteric hip fractures requiring operative treatment at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. Although enrollment is open to adults aged 18 years and older, the study population is expected to consist predominantly of older adults.

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* Does treatment with suzetrigine as part of multimodal pain therapy reduce postoperative opioid consumption, measured as morphine milligram equivalents (MME), during the index hospitalization through 72 hours after surgery or hospital discharge, whichever occurs first?
* Does suzetrigine provide effective postoperative pain control and have an acceptable safety and tolerability profile in adults undergoing hip fracture surgery? Researchers will compare participants receiving suzetrigine plus standard multimodal analgesia with matched historical BIDMC patients who underwent similar hip fracture surgery between 2020 and 2025 and received standard multimodal analgesia without suzetrigine. Historical controls will be matched on factors including age, sex, fracture type, surgery type, surgeon, ASA class, opioid-naïve status, regional anesthesia, and relevant comorbidities.

Participants in the prospective study will:

* Receive a 100-mg oral loading dose of suzetrigine before surgery, followed by 50 mg orally every 12 hours for up to 14 days or until pain resolves, whichever occurs first.
* Receive standard multimodal pain management, which may include acetaminophen, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications when appropriate, regional anesthesia, and rescue opioid medication as clinically needed.
* Complete pain assessments during hospitalization and at follow-up time points, with opioid use recorded and converted to MME.
* Complete follow-up assessments at approximately Days 7, 14, and 28 after surgery, including pain, medication use, adverse events, treatment adherence, and patient-reported outcomes.
* Record study medication use, missed doses, rescue opioid use, and adverse events after hospital discharge when applicable.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Opioid Consumption Rate
Cumulative Postoperative Opioid Consumption
title: Suzetrigine (Journavx) as Multimodal Therapy for Pain Management in Adults Undergoing Surgery for Hip Fracture

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare the effects of McGill Stabilization Exercises and Pilates on pain, muscle thickness, lumbar flexibility, and disability in adults aged 30-50 years with chronic non-specific low back pain.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do McGill Stabilization Exercises and Pilates reduce pain and disability in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain?
* Do these interventions improve lumbar flexibility and transversus abdominis muscle thickness? Researchers will compare the McGill Stabilization Exercises group with the Pilates group to determine which intervention produces greater improvements in pain, muscle thickness, lumbar flexibility, and disability.

Participants will:

* Receive either McGill Stabilization Exercises or Pilates, according to their assigned study group.
* Receive transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) and hot-pack therapy before the exercise intervention.
* Attend treatment sessions twice weekly for six weeks, for a total of 12 sessions.
* Complete assessments of pain intensity, disability, lumbar flexibility, and transversus abdominis muscle thickness at baseline and after six weeks.

brief_summary: This is a single-center, prospective, parallel randomized controlled trial. A total of 180 patients aged 18-75 years undergoing elective laparoscopic colorectal surgery with ASA physical status Ⅰ-Ⅲ will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to ciprofol group, remimazolam group or propofol group. All patients receive standardized background anesthesia regimen including dexmedetomidine, sufentanil, rocuronium and remifentanil. The primary outcome is the QoR-15 score at postoperative day 1. Secondary outcomes include intraoperative hemodynamic parameters, anesthesia recovery indicators, postoperative VAS pain scores, opioid consumption and perioperative adverse events. The study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University (approval number: 2023-KY-0137-002). Written informed consent will be obtained from each participant before enrollment.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether QLS4131, a BCMA/GPRC5D/CD3 trispecific antibody, can improve treatment outcomes when combined with isatuximab in adults with newly diagnosed primary plasma cell leukemia (pPCL). The study will also evaluate the safety of this treatment combination.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How many participants achieve measurable residual disease (MRD) negativity after 9 treatment cycles?
* What side effects occur during treatment with QLS4131 combined with isatuximab?
* How many participants respond to treatment, and how many achieve a complete response?
* How many participants achieve sustained MRD negativity?
* How long do participants remain free from disease progression, and how long do they survive after starting treatment?

All participants will receive the study treatment. There is no comparison group in this study.

Participants will:

* Receive QLS4131 by subcutaneous injection together with intravenous isatuximab in 28-day treatment cycles.
* Undergo regular blood tests, bone marrow examinations, and disease assessments to monitor treatment response and safety.
* Undergo peripheral blood stem cell mobilization and collection after the first 3 treatment cycles, if appropriate.
* Be monitored throughout the study for side effects, including adverse events and serious adverse events.

brief_summary:
FRAIL-CARE is a prospective, multicentre, non-profit, low-intervention pilot feasibility study conducted in four Maugeri Scientific Clinical Institutes (IRCCS) in Lombardy, Italy. It will enrol 40 frail patients older than 65 years who take five or more drugs every day and are discharged home from cardiac, neurological or pulmonary rehabilitation, oncology or internal medicine units.

After discharge, patients and their caregivers use a CE-marked digital health solution made of a smartphone app, a portable connected monitoring device and a clinician dashboard. Remote Specialist Operations Centres (COS), staffed by trained case managers, follow symptoms, vital signs and alerts and call patients at least once a week. The Poison Control Centre of Pavia acts as the emergency centre outside COS hours, for urgent clinical questions, drug interactions and treatment changes. In addition, blood concentrations of prescribed drugs that are not usually covered by therapeutic drug monitoring are measured at discharge, at 3 and 6 months, and whenever an adverse reaction, lack of efficacy or interaction is suspected.

The main aim is to evaluate the impact of this integrated home care model on quality of life (EQ-5D-5L). Secondary aims are to assess usability and acceptability of the technology (System Usability Scale), adherence to therapy (MARS-5), early detection of critical clinical events and potentially toxic drug levels, and the number of dropouts. Each patient is followed for 6 months. The results will provide a basis for welfare policies supporting frail patients.
conditions: Polypharmacy (People Under Treatment With 5 or More Drugs)
interventions: Remote monitoring by Specialist Operations Centres
Blood drug concentration monitoring beyond routine TDM
primary_outcomes: Change in health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5L)

brief_summary:
This study will examine whether art-based group reminiscence therapy can improve psychological resilience and joy of living in adults aged 60 years and older. Psychological resilience means being able to cope with and recover from difficult experiences. Reminiscence involves remembering and sharing experiences from the past. The study will also examine whether any improvements remain one month after the program ends.

Approximately 50 older adults attending the Tazelenme University program at Suleyman Demirel University in Isparta, Türkiye, will participate. Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups, with approximately 25 people in each group.

Participants in the intervention group will attend eight sessions over four weeks, with two sessions per week. Each session will last 60-90 minutes and take place in a small group of 8-10 people. A trained psychiatric nurse will guide the sessions. Participants will share memories and take part in creative activities using photographs, music, and art materials. Topics will include childhood, family life, school years, relationships, meaningful life roles, pleasant memories, personal strengths, and lessons learned throughout life.

Participants in the control group will continue their usual social activities without receiving the study program during the study period. After the study is completed, they will be offered the opportunity to take part in the reminiscence program if they wish.

Participants in both groups will complete questionnaires about psychological resilience and joy of living at three time points: before the program begins, after the four-week program ends, and one month later. Researchers will compare changes between the two groups to assess the effects of the program.
primary_outcomes: Psychological Resilience
Joy of Living
title: Effects of Art-Based Group Reminiscence Therapy on Resilience and Joy of Living in Older Adults

There are no medications that can prevent OIRD. Pre-clinical studies provided evidence that intranasal (administered via a nasal spray) oxytocin may prevent and treat OIRD without interfering with pain control.

brief_summary: Research shows that heavy drinking patterns are linked to many harmful consequences including death, sexual assault, risky sexual behavior, and drug use. Given such harmful consequences, it is important to identify the risk-factors for heavy "in-the-moment" drinking. This study examines a potent, socially motivated trigger to problem drinking-namely, social rejection. In the present study, we employ a between-subjects experimental design with a sample of young adults (N=152; aged 21-25 years; 50% female) to examine how social rejection experiences are associated with drinking behavior as a function of attachment anxiety, changes in pain experience, and self-control.
primary_outcomes: Alcohol Consumption
title: Does Attachment Anxiety Moderate the Influence of Social Rejection on Alcohol Use Among Young Adults?

brief_summary:
60 million people in Europe have diabetes (DM) and up to 34% (20.4 million) of them are at risk of developing diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) in their lifetime (1). However, current primary and community care is suboptimal with 40% of DFUs recurring within a year. Path Active (PA) is a digital health tool composed of smart insoles and a Bluetooth-connected app, which remotely monitors users' DFU risk, reducing their reliance on institutionalised care.

This project will use interdisciplinary approaches to assess PA's ability to strengthen primary and community care systems (Subtopic 1) in culturally and socioeconomically diverse settings. We will take an ecosystem approach, incorporating multiple stakeholders including end-user patients,healthcare professionals, policy makers and potential commercial partners, investigating PA through economic, social, and clinical lenses. The project will pilot PA in \>100 individuals across 3 different countries (Canada, Denmark, and Spain) over 18 months. This will allow us to carry out:

* Implementation research: Mapping PA implementation in diverse care settings, identifying local barriers to PA's adoption and necessary changes to promote PA integration into community care.
* Service and ICT research: End user-testing to facilitate iterative design improvements, ensuring PA is culturally appropriate.
* Health economics and policy research: Investigate international policy impact on the health economics surrounding PA and inform PA's market plan for different health systems.
* Pilots: Gather evidence on PA's effectiveness in preventing DFUs and investigate/tackle any potential efficacy differences between cultures.
* Business development: Scale up PA production and map potential stakeholders in member sites.

Overall, STRIDE-COM represents a significant step toward integrating innovative digital health solutions into primary care across Europe/Canada, establishing a replicable model for wearable technologies.
interventions: Path Active™, a smart insole system designed to reduce the risk of plantar ulceration in patients with diabetic foot disease
primary_outcomes: Incidence and time to first Ulceration:
Quality of Life
Ulcer Location
Adherence
Foot-Care Behaviour
title: Better Care Closer to Home: Enhancing Primary and Community Care

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled Phase III clinical trial, aiming to evaluate the efficacy and safety of HB0025 combined with chemotherapy (paclitaxel plus carboplatin) versus placebo combined with chemotherapy (paclitaxel plus carboplatin) as a first-line treatment for advanced (Stage III/IV) or recurrent proficient Mismatch Repair Endometrial Cancer（pMMR EC).

The trial will take progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR) as the primary endpoint, and plans to enroll approximately 333 participants. After being eligible for screening, participants will be randomly assigned to the study arms at a ratio of 2:1 to receive either HB0025 combined with chemotherapy (experimental group) or placebo combined with chemotherapy (control group). Both regimens will be administered once every 3 weeks (Q3W). After completing 6 cycles of combination treatment, patients will enter the maintenance therapy phase with HB0025 or placebo (Q3W) only. The treatment will last until intolerable toxicity occurs, disease progression, lost to follow up or death, withdrawal of consent, pre-scheduled study treatment are completed, receiving new anticancer therapy or sponsor discontinue the study, whichever comes first.
primary_outcomes: Progression-free survival (PFS)
title: HB0025-C-0301: A Study to Investigate HB0025 Combined With Chemotherapy as First-Line Treatment for Advanced or Recurrent MMR-proficient Endometrial Cancer

brief_summary:
Contemporary ART fails to eradicate the HIV-1 virus from PWH, resulting in a rebound in viremia within days to weeks after cessation of ART. Evidence indicates that disparities in biological and sociocultural characteristics between resource-limited and resource-privileged settings affect treatment outcomes. Consequently, resource-constrained settings must possess the capability to comprehend the mechanisms and drivers of HIV persistence, as well as to devise and evaluate therapies for HIV cure or prolonged remission within local populations. The investigators will employ genomic, metabolomics, and transcriptomics to analyze samples from a successful therapeutic trial we conducted in Brazil, a resource-constrained country, to identify and investigate mechanisms of HIV persistence and we will employ novel latency-reversal agents and advanced in vivo cell therapy.

The clinical trial the investigators will conduct will employ a multifaceted intervention strategy to achieve HIV remission through intensified ART to reduce residual HIV replication, a novel combination of latency reversal agents (LRA), and cell therapy utilizing autologous dendritic cells infused with autologous HIV peptides.

RHD is a sequela of \*Streptococcus pyogenes\* infection, which can originate from tonsillitis or from impetigo secondary to a scabies infestation.

brief_summary:
People with non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma may remain at high risk of cancer recurrence even after surgery has removed all visible disease. This study will test whether treatment after surgery with serplulimab plus fruquintinib improves outcomes compared with observation alone.

This is a multicenter, randomized, open-label Phase III study. Approximately 108 adults will be assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive the drug combination or observation. Participants in both groups will undergo scheduled follow-up. The main measure is the proportion of participants who remain free of recurrence two years after randomization. The study will also assess recurrence-free survival over time, overall survival, safety, and exploratory biomarkers.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a mouthwash made from thyme (Thymus vulgaris in its scientific name) helps improve gum health in people with plaque-induced gingivitis. The mouthwash will be compared with Chlorhexidine mouthwash and a placebo (a mouthwash that does not contain the active ingredient being tested).

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does Thymus vulgaris mouthwash improve gum health and lower plaque buildup and gum bleeding?
* Does it change the levels of substances in saliva linked to gum inflammation and tissue damage?
* What side effects do participants experience, and how do they rate their experience with the mouthwash?

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: Thymus vulgaris mouthwash, 0.12% Chlorhexidine mouthwash, or placebo. They will:

* Rinse with 10 mL of their assigned mouthwash twice daily for one minute each time.
* Have their gum health checked at the start of the study, after two weeks, and after one month.
* Provide saliva samples at each visit for testing.
* Report any side effects and share their experience with the mouthwash.

To help ensure a fair comparison, the mouthwashes will be provided in identical containers with coded labels. Neither participants nor the examiner will know which mouthwash each participant receives until the study is completed and the results are analyzed.
primary_outcomes: Bleeding on Probing
title: Efficacy of Thymus Vulgaris Mouthwash in the Management of Biofilm-Induced Gingivitis

brief_summary:
Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a common non-cancerous enlargement of the prostate gland in aging men that causes bothersome lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), including frequent urination, weak urinary stream, and difficulty emptying the bladder. Prostatic artery embolization (PAE) is a minimally invasive, image-guided catheter procedure that blocks blood flow to the prostate, leading to gland shrinkage and symptom relief. While traditional PAE utilizes particulate agents, N-butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA / Histoacryl) glue is a liquid embolic material that may offer advantages such as shorter procedural duration, lower radiation exposure, and permanent vascular occlusion.

The purpose of this prospective, single-arm study is to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and clinical efficacy of using Histoacryl glue mixed with Lipiodol (1:8 dilution ratio) during prostatic artery embolization in men with symptomatic BPH who have failed or cannot tolerate medical therapy.

All enrolled participants will undergo PAE with the Histoacryl glue mixture. Participants will be monitored for procedural safety and followed up at 1 month and 3 months post-procedure. Follow-up assessments include urinary symptom improvement using the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), quality of life (QoL) ratings, post-void residual urine volume, prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels, pelvic imaging to measure prostate volume reduction, and monitoring for any procedure-related complications.
interventions: Prostatic Artery Embolization with N-butyl Cyanoacrylate
primary_outcomes: Clinical Success Rate
title: Prostatic Artery Embolization Using Histoacryl as a Novel Embolizing Agent for Treatment of BPH

brief_summary: This study will compare three methods of activating the final irrigation solution in reducing living bacteria inside the root canals of teeth that require root canal retreatment because of apical periodontitis, an inflammatory condition of the tissues around the root tip. The three methods are photon-induced photoacoustic streaming (PIPS), shock wave-enhanced emission photoacoustic streaming (SWEEPS), and passive ultrasonic irrigation (PUI). Ninety adults requiring retreatment of a single-rooted, single-canal tooth will be randomly assigned to three groups; all treatment steps other than the activation method will be identical. Root canal samples will be collected at several stages of the single-visit treatment, and living bacteria will be counted using laboratory cultures. In addition, real-time PCR will be used to measure the relative amount of Enterococcus faecalis DNA compared with total bacterial DNA. Because PCR cannot distinguish living from dead bacteria, these molecular results will be interpreted as complementary to the culture findings.

This prospective, observational, self-controlled study aims to compare the glottic view obtained in the standard sniffing position with that obtained in the 45° LeHeR position in the same adult patients undergoing elective surgery under general anesthesia with direct laryngoscopy. Glottic view will be graded with the modified Cormack-Lehane classification and the Percentage of Glottic Opening (POGO) score. Intubation difficulty, need for additional maneuvers or adjuncts, hemodynamic changes, and airway trauma will also be recorded.

brief_summary:
The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on anaerobic performance and cardiorespiratory responses in alpine skiing athletes. The study included 40 male alpine skiers aged 16-22 years residing in Bitlis, Türkiye, with 20 participants in the experimental group and 20 in the control group.

Throughout the study, all participants continued similar regular alpine skiing training programs to control for potential differences in training volume and fitness levels. Considering the competition schedule, the intervention period was designed to last 12 weeks. During this period, the experimental group performed high-intensity interval training twice per week in addition to their regular skiing training, while the control group continued their regular training program. Exercise intensity during HIIT sessions was maintained at 85-95% of the athletes' maximum heart rate.

Cardiorespiratory performance was evaluated using a maximal exercise test to assess maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max), respiratory quotient (RQ), maximum heart rate (HRmax), and oxygen uptake per heartbeat (VO₂/HR). Anaerobic performance was assessed using the Wingate anaerobic power test, including peak power, average power, minimum power, power drop, and total energy output.

The Shapiro-Wilk test was used to assess data normality. Paired-samples t-tests were used for within-group pretest-posttest comparisons, while independent-samples t-tests were used for between-group comparisons. The statistical significance level was set at p \< 0.05.

The study was designed to evaluate the potential contribution of a 12-week HIIT program to anaerobic performance and cardiorespiratory adaptations in alpine skiing athletes.

Keywords: Alpine skiing, high-intensity interval training, anaerobic power, VO₂max.
interventions: Regular Alpine Skiing and Strength Training
primary_outcomes: Change in Peak Anaerobic Power
Change in Maximal Oxygen Uptake (VO2max)
Change in Maximum Heart Rate (HRmax)
Change in Total Energy Output
title: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) on Physiological Responses in Alpine Skiers

brief_summary: Every year, thousands of Canadians receive life-saving, cost-effective organ transplants, while thousands more still wait or die because not enough organs are available. Patients with non-recoverable illnesses, who are undergoing withdrawal of life sustaining measures, can donate their organs when they die by a process called donation after death determination by circulatory criteria (DCC), previously known as donation after circulatory determined death (DCD). However, over 30% of all DCC attempts are unsuccessful because patients do not die within the time frame required for healthy organ retrieval and prolonged exposure to low oxygen during the dying process renders organs unsuitable for transplantation. Predicting successful DCC is difficult and leads to uncertainty in the clinical community. To address this issue, the investigators have developed a clinical decision support tool called Donation Advisor (DA) designed to assist with donation and transplantation decision making. The investigators are ready to implement DA in at least four hospitals in Ontario and evaluate its impact in these hospitals. An additional hospital will be participating solely as a transplant centre. The investigators believe use of DA will reduce unsuccessful DCC attempts, enhance family experience of donation, optimize system costs, and improve transplant outcomes.

brief_summary:
Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder that disrupts a person's regular sleep-wake cycle. It causes extreme sleepiness during the day (called excessive daytime sleepiness \[EDS\]), where a person may fall asleep without warning. Narcolepsy Type 1 (NT1) is a form of the condition in which people also have sudden, unexpected muscle weakness while staying conscious (called cataplexy). The usual care for NT1 focuses on managing symptoms and improving the sleep and wake cycle. It pays special attention to daytime sleepiness. Information on treatment use and related effects in adults with NT1 is limited. This study aims to collect such information and help fill this gap.

The main aim of this study is to better understand how adults with NT1 are treated in real life, why treatment changes happen and how different treatment choices (both medicines and non-medicine strategies) affect symptoms, cataplexy and quality of life over time. The study also aims to learn more about adults with NT1, how they are diagnosed, how their treatment works, and how often they need medical care. It will also record how satisfied they are with treatment and how NT1 affects their symptoms, daily life, and quality of life over time.
